definition_zh: 珍贵的；宝贵的；贵重的；值钱的；娇贵做作的；（precious little）少得可怜
definition_en: worth a great deal because of rarity, love or beauty; costly in material terms; over-refined in manner; and used before little or few to mean almost none
core_image: 掌心托着一枚旧顶针，金属已被磨得发亮
scene: 老人从抽屉最里层取出一只用手帕包着的小盒，盒里躺着一枚褪色的顶针。She never wore the ring because it was too precious to risk losing.
sceneCN: 这里 precious 指「珍贵得不敢轻易动用」（第 1 个义项：因情感或稀有而宝贵）；句意为她从不戴那枚戒指，因为太珍贵，怕弄丢。图中可辨识物件：抽屉深处的手帕、褪色的顶针、磨亮的金属。

pos.zh: 珍贵的；宝贵的；贵重的；娇贵做作的

derivatives.zh: 由 precious 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「珍贵地；做作地」
由 precious 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「珍贵；矫饰」
由前缀 semi-（半）与 precious 复合而成，义为「半宝石的」

senses.title: Worth a great deal to someone
senses.definition: worth a great deal because it is rare, loved or impossible to replace
senses.definitionCN: 因稀有、被珍爱或无法替代而具有很大价值
senses.example: Her grandmother's letters are the most precious thing she owns.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母的信是她最珍视的东西。
senses.why: The Latin noun pretium named the value set on a thing, and its adjective pretiosus described whatever carried that value; English kept the worth and let the money side go.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 pretium 本指给一件东西定下的价值，形容词 pretiosus 就用来形容带着这份价值的东西；英语留下「价值」这一面，把「价钱」那一面让给了 price。

senses.title: Costly because of the material
senses.definition: made of a material that costs a lot, such as gold, silver or a fine stone
senses.definitionCN: 由金、银或上等宝石等昂贵材料制成
senses.example: The crown is set with precious stones brought from the east.
senses.exampleCN: 这顶王冠镶着从东方运来的宝石。
senses.why: A second step inside the same root: pretium also meant the money a thing costs, so the adjective could describe objects whose material alone makes them expensive, not only things loved for memory.
senses.whyCN: 同一词根的第二步：pretium 也能指一件东西所值的钱，于是这个形容词可以形容单凭材料就昂贵的物件，而不只是因回忆而被珍爱的东西。

senses.title: Over-refined in manner or style
senses.definition: too delicate, refined or fussy in behaviour, taste or style, so that it seems affected
senses.definitionCN: 举止、品味或风格过于精细挑剔，显得做作
senses.example: He has a precious way of holding his cup that amuses his friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他端杯子的样子讲究得有点做作，朋友们都拿这个打趣。
senses.why: Value set too high turns into a criticism: a person who treats small things as treasures is called precious in a mocking tone, so the word moves from the object to the attitude.
senses.whyCN: 把价值定得太高就会变成批评：一个把小事情当宝贝的人，会被带着讥讽地叫作 precious，词义于是从「物件」转到「态度」。

senses.title: Almost none, in precious little and precious few
senses.titleCN: （用于 precious little、precious few）少得可怜
senses.definition: used before little or few to stress that there is far less of something than is wanted
senses.definitionCN: 用在 little 或 few 前，强调某物的数量比所需少得多
senses.example: There is precious little time left before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 离截止只剩少得可怜的一点时间。
senses.why: This ironic use grows out of the same scale: a precious thing should be plentiful, so calling a tiny amount precious underlines how little of it there is.
senses.whyCN: 这种反讽用法长在同一杆价值尺度上：珍贵的东西本该充足，偏说那一点点很「珍贵」，反而把「少」强调出来。

intro.en: Precious and price are twins from one Latin noun, pretium. English sent price down the market road and precious down the road of worth, which is why the two now feel unrelated.
intro.cn: precious 与 price 是同一个拉丁名词 pretium 生下的一对双胞胎。英语让 price 走上买卖的路，让 precious 走上价值的另一条路，所以今天两者听起来毫不相干。

items.en: Pretium meant the price or value assigned to a thing, and it could name both the money paid and the worth people believed a thing had.
items.cn: pretium 指给一件东西定下的价钱或价值，既能指付出的钱，也能指人们认为它值多少。

items.en: Pretiosus was built on pretium and described something of great worth, especially costly stones, metals and cloth.
items.cn: pretiosus 由 pretium 构成，形容价值很高的东西，尤指昂贵的宝石、金属与织物。

items.en: Old French took the adjective as precios, meaning costly and highly valued, and passed it to English in the medieval period.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 precios，意为昂贵的、极受重视的，并在中世纪传入英语。

items.en: Middle English precious kept the sense of great worth and began to be used for things valued for love rather than for money.
items.cn: 中古英语的 precious 保留「价值极高」的意思，并开始用于因感情而非金钱而宝贵的东西。

items.en: Modern English holds the split: price names what a thing costs, precious names what it is worth to someone, and the ironic precious little adds a third shade.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个分叉固定下来：price 指一件东西要多少钱，precious 指它对某人值多少，反讽的 precious little 又添了第三层色彩。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the family that grew from Latin pretium; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for things people value.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语 pretium 长出来的同族词；近义组收人们用来形容「看重之物」的形容词。

entries.definition: The money a seller asks for something; it comes from the same Latin noun but took the commercial path.
entries.definitionCN: 卖方为一物索要的钱；与本词同出一个拉丁名词，但走的是买卖那条路。

entries.definition: To recognise the value of something, or to rise in value.
entries.definitionCN: 认识到某物的价值；也指升值。

entries.definition: A judgement of how much something is worth.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物价值的评估。

entries.definition: The quality of being precious, or of being over-refined.
entries.definitionCN: 珍贵的性质；也指做作讲究。

entries.definition: Worth a lot of money or of great use.
entries.definitionCN: 值很多钱的；很有用的。

entries.definition: Expensive, or causing loss and damage.
entries.definitionCN: 昂贵的；也指造成损失和破坏的。

entries.definition: Loved and kept with care over a long time.
entries.definitionCN: 长期被珍爱、被小心保存的。

entries.definition: Much loved, and in British English also expensive.
entries.definitionCN: 深受喜爱的；英式英语里也指昂贵的。

normalIntro.en: One Latin noun of value splits into a market word and a word of worth; the English adjective then climbs from treasure to taste, and finally to irony.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示价值的拉丁名词分成了市场词与价值词；英语形容词再从珍宝爬到品味，最后落到反讽。

normal.en: Pretium gives both price and precious, so the twins are cousins: one counts coins, the other counts what the coins cannot buy.
normal.cn: pretium 同时生出 price 与 precious，这对双胞胎是表亲：一个数钱，一个数钱买不到的东西。

normal.en: Precious metal and precious stone are fixed phrases: the material itself is the value.
normal.cn: precious metal 与 precious stone 是固定搭配，材料本身就是价值。

normal.en: Precious little means very little, and the word is doing the opposite of its usual job there.
normal.cn: precious little 意为「少得可怜」，在这里这个词做的正好是它平常相反的事。

normal.en: Preciousness adds -ness to name the quality, and it can be praise or a complaint about fussiness.
normal.cn: preciousness 加 -ness 表示性质，既可以是称赞，也可以是在抱怨过于讲究。

normal.en: Semiprecious keeps semi-, half, for stones such as amethyst that are valued but not in the first rank.
normal.cn: semiprecious 保留 semi-（半）这个成分，用于紫水晶这类有价值但不算头等的宝石。

abstract.en: Value has two doors: what a thing costs and what a thing means, and English gave each door its own word.
abstract.cn: 价值有两扇门：一件东西值多少钱，以及它意味着什么；英语给每扇门配了一个词。

abstract.en: When the word is used as an insult, it is because caring too much about small refinements looks like a false scale of value.
abstract.cn: 这个词用来损人时，是因为过分在意细枝末节，看起来像一杆失准的价值秤。

abstract.en: Precious little is a small joke built into the language: the more precious the thing, the sharper the complaint that there is almost none.
abstract.cn: precious little 是语言里自带的一个小玩笑：东西越珍贵，抱怨「几乎没有」就越扎人。

examples.en: Her grandmother's letters are the most precious thing she owns.
examples.cn: 祖母的信是她最珍视的东西。

examples.en: The box was inlaid with precious stones.
examples.cn: 这只盒子镶着宝石。

examples.en: There is precious little evidence for that claim.
examples.cn: 那个说法几乎没有证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普雷舍斯」——贵重东西捧在手里，舍不得放下；precious 就是珍贵的。

root: 拉丁语 pretium（价钱、价值）→ 形容词 pretiosus（价值高的）→ 古法语 precios → 英语 precious。同族的 price 走的是「买卖价钱」那一路，precious 走的是「本身可贵」这一路，两者同源而语义分叉。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow one scale of value: a treasured thing, an expensive material, a fussy attitude that overvalues small things, and an ironic phrase that turns value into scarcity.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项沿着同一杆价值尺度展开：被珍爱之物、昂贵材料、把小节看得过重的做作，以及把「珍贵」翻成「稀缺」的反讽说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn thimble resting in an open palm, its metal polished by years of use.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚磨旧的顶针躺在摊开的手掌上，金属被多年使用磨得发亮。

branches.en: a ring kept in a handkerchief and never worn
branches.cn: 手帕里那枚从不戴的戒指

branches.en: stones prised out of a crown to be weighed
branches.cn: 从王冠上撬下、拿去称重的宝石

branches.en: one value measured by love and one by money
branches.cn: 一份价值用感情量，一份用钱量

branches.en: a cup lifted by the handle with two fingers
branches.cn: 用两根手指捏着杯柄端起的杯子

branches.en: a clock with almost no time left on it
branches.cn: 只剩一点点时间的钟

intro.en: A Latin noun of value, an adjective suffix that says full of it, and a French reshaping carry the word into English; -ly and -ness then build the adverb and the noun.
intro.cn: 一个表示价值的拉丁名词、一个表示「充满」的形容词后缀，以及法语的一次改写，把这个词带进英语；-ly 与 -ness 再分别造出副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Pretium and its adjective pretiosus are well recorded, and the verb appretiare valued a thing; English inherited the family through French.
latinIntro.cn: pretium 及其形容词 pretiosus 都有清楚的记录，动词 appretiare 意为「估价」；英语经法语继承了这一族词。

items.meaning: in a precious or affected way

definition_zh: 使沉淀；使突然发生；促成；猛地落下；仓促的；沉淀物
definition_en: to cause a solid to form out of a solution, or to make an event happen suddenly and too soon
core_image: 澄清的溶液里浮着看不见的微粒，一滴试剂落下，它们忽然结成白色小块沉到杯底
scene: 实验员往澄清的溶液里滴入试剂，杯底很快出现白色粉末。A few drops of reagent precipitate a white powder at the bottom of the beaker.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「使溶解的物质析出成固体」（第 1 个义项：化学上使固体析出）；句意为几滴试剂使烧杯底部析出白色粉末。

pos.zh: 使沉淀；使突然发生；促成
沉淀；猛地落下
仓促的；鲁莽的
沉淀物

senses.title: Cause a solid to form
senses.definition: to cause a dissolved substance to come out of a solution as a solid
senses.definitionCN: 使溶解的物质从溶液中以固体形态出来
senses.example: A few drops of reagent precipitate a white powder at the bottom of the beaker.
senses.exampleCN: 几滴试剂使烧杯底部析出白色粉末。
senses.why: The Latin verb means 'throw headlong'; a solid that was invisibly dissolved is suddenly thrown down out of the liquid.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「头朝下抛落」；原本看不见地溶解着的固体，忽然被从液体里抛了下来。

senses.title: Settle out of a liquid
senses.definition: of a solid, to separate from a solution and settle
senses.definitionCN: 固体从溶液中分离并沉降下来
senses.example: The salt precipitated out as the water evaporated.
senses.exampleCN: 水分蒸发时，盐沉淀析出。
senses.why: When no agent is named, the subject is the solid itself doing the falling, so the verb turns intransitive.
senses.whyCN: 当不点明施动者时，主语就是固体自己在落下，于是动词转为不及物。

senses.title: Make an event happen suddenly
senses.definition: to cause an event to happen suddenly or earlier than expected
senses.definitionCN: 使事件突然、或比预期更早地发生
senses.example: The border incident precipitated a full diplomatic crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 边境事件骤然引发了一场全面的外交危机。
senses.why: A crisis that was suspended in the future is thrown into the present; the downward image becomes a jump in time.
senses.whyCN: 原本悬在未来的危机被抛进现在；向下的意象变成了时间上的跳跃。

senses.title: Hasten a process
senses.definition: to make a process happen faster than it otherwise would
senses.definitionCN: 使某个过程比原本更快地发生
senses.example: Poor drainage precipitated the collapse of the embankment.
senses.exampleCN: 排水不良加速了堤岸的崩塌。
senses.why: This is the same causal push as the previous sense, but the focus is on speed rather than suddenness.
senses.whyCN: 这与上一个义项是同一种因果推力，只是焦点在速度而非突然性。

senses.title: Hasty or rash
senses.definition: done too quickly, without proper thought
senses.definitionCN: 做得过快、缺乏周全考虑的
senses.example: They regretted their precipitate sale of the land.
senses.exampleCN: 他们后悔仓促卖掉了那块地。
senses.why: An adjective born from 'headlong': a person who acts this way is diving before looking.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词出自「头朝下」：这样行事的人还没看清就往下栽。

senses.title: The solid deposit
senses.definition: the solid substance produced by precipitation, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 沉淀过程产生的固体物质，作名词使用
senses.example: Filter off the precipitate and wash it twice.
senses.exampleCN: 把沉淀物滤出并洗涤两次。
senses.why: The process and its product share one form: what has been thrown down is the precipitate.
senses.whyCN: 过程与产物共用一个形式：被抛下来的东西就是 precipitate。

senses.title: Throw down headlong
senses.definition: in older writing, to throw a person or thing down from a height
senses.definitionCN: 在旧时文本中，把人或物从高处抛下
senses.example: The old account says the guards precipitated him from the tower.
senses.exampleCN: 旧记载说卫兵把他从塔上抛了下去。
senses.why: This literal bodily sense is the source of all the others and now survives mainly in historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个字面的身体义是其余义项的源头，如今主要保存在历史文本中。

senses.title: Fall as rain or snow
senses.definition: of water, to fall from the sky as rain, snow or hail
senses.definitionCN: 指水从天空以雨、雪或冰雹的形式落下
senses.example: Moist air rose, cooled, and began to precipitate over the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 湿空气抬升、冷却，开始在山丘上空降水。
senses.why: The meteorological use keeps the literal falling but drops the human agent; the sky itself is the thrower.
senses.whyCN: 气象用法保留了字面的落下，却去掉了人的施动者；抛落者变成了天空本身。

intro.en: Precipitate came into English from Latin as a learned word and then split into chemical and everyday uses. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: precipitate 作为学术词从拉丁语进入英语，随后分出化学义与日常义。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Latin praecipitare meant 'to throw down headlong, to hasten', with the participle praecipitatus 'thrown down'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 praecipitare 意为「头朝下抛落、加速促成」，分词为 praecipitatus「被抛下的」。

items.en: The verb is prae- 'before, forth' plus caput 'head'. A person or thing goes over an edge and falls head first.
items.cn: 该动词是 prae-「在前、向前」加 caput「头」。人或物越过边缘，头朝下坠落。

items.en: Alchemy and medicine borrowed the word for a substance settling out of a liquid, since the solid seemed to fall out of the solution.
items.cn: 炼金术与医学借这个词指物质从液体中沉降出来，因为固体看起来像是从溶液里掉了出来。

items.en: The adjective developed the sense 'hasty, rash', judging conduct by the same headlong image.
items.cn: 形容词发展出「仓促、鲁莽」义，用同一个头朝下的意象来评判行为。

items.en: Chemistry fixed the verb and noun for solid formation, while journalism kept the sense of causing an event too soon.
items.cn: 十九至二十世纪，化学把这个动词与名词固定为固体析出义，新闻写作则保留了「使事件过早发生」的用法。

note.en: Group one separates the look-alikes, including two true relatives; group two holds verbs with overlapping meanings.
note.cn: 第一组分辨形近词，其中两个是真正的同族词；第二组是意义重叠的动词。

entries.definition: To take part. It goes back to Latin particeps 'sharing', with a different root; only the ending sounds similar.
entries.definitionCN: 参加。它追溯到拉丁语 particeps「分享」，词根不同；只有词尾听起来相近。

entries.definition: Very steep, or done with too much haste. It is a true relative, so the -ous ending marks an adjective, not a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 陡峭的，或过于仓促的。它是真正的同族词，-ous 词尾表示形容词而不是动词。

entries.definition: A cliff or a dangerous position. It is a true relative from Latin praecipitium, and it names the edge rather than the fall.
entries.definitionCN: 悬崖或险境。它是出自拉丁语 praecipitium 的真正同族词，指边缘而不是坠落。

entries.definition: To make something happen sooner; it stresses speed and carries no idea of falling.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事更早发生；强调速度，不含坠落的意象。

entries.definition: To cause an event to begin, usually a sudden reaction; it images a catch being released, not a body falling.
entries.definitionCN: 引发事件开始，通常指突然反应；意象是扳机被松开，而不是身体坠落。

entries.definition: Material that has settled or been left on a surface; it can be the result of precipitation but is not the chemical process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 沉降或留在表面上的物质；可以是沉淀的结果，但不指化学过程本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin pieces and real chemistry usage, no invented links.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：使用真实的拉丁构件与真实的化学用法，不编造联系。

normal.en: prae- 'before' + capit- 'head': the word pictures someone diving over an edge, head first.
normal.cn: prae-「在前」+ capit-「头」：这个词描绘一个人越过边缘、头朝下栽下去。

normal.en: precipitate is both verb and noun in chemistry: the reagent precipitates the solid, and the solid is the precipitate.
normal.cn: precipitate 在化学里既是动词又是名词：试剂把固体沉淀出来，那个固体就是沉淀物。

normal.en: precipitation is the noun of the process, built with -ation, exactly like preparation and evaporation.
normal.cn: precipitation 是用 -ation 构成的过程名词，与 preparation、evaporation 完全同构。

normal.en: precipitous keeps the same root but describes a cliff, so steepness and haste are two readings of 'headlong'.
normal.cn: precipitous 保留同一词根却形容悬崖，于是「陡」与「急」是 headlong 的两种读法。

normal.en: a precipitate decision is a decision made as if falling: fast, uncontrolled, hard to stop.
normal.cn: a precipitate decision 是像坠落一样做出的决定：快、失控、难停住。

abstract.en: Abstractly, precipitate is any force that removes something from a suspended state: a reagent, a border incident, a bad decision.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，precipitate 是任何把某物从悬浮状态中移除的力：一滴试剂、一起边境事件、一个糟糕的决定。

abstract.en: The common shape is a threshold crossed too fast, after which the thing can no longer stay where it was.
abstract.cn: 共同的形状是一个被过快越过的门槛，越过之后，那东西再也留不在原处。

abstract.en: So the word moves between beakers, calendars and personalities without changing its geometry: over the edge, head first.
abstract.cn: 于是这个词在烧杯、日历与性格之间移动，而几何不变：越过边缘，头朝下。

examples.en: Cooling the mixture will precipitate the dissolved crystals.
examples.cn: 让混合物冷却会使溶解的晶体沉淀出来。

examples.en: The announcement precipitated a sharp fall in the currency.
examples.cn: 这项声明导致货币急剧下跌。

examples.en: It was a precipitate move that no one had time to review.
examples.cn: 那是一个谁都没时间复核的仓促举动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆读「pre-（前）+ cipit（头）」：头朝前栽下去 → precipitate 使沉淀、使骤然发生

root: 拉丁语 praecipitare「头朝下抛落；加速」← prae-「向前」+ caput「头」；分词 praecipitatus 进入英语为 precipitate，与 precipitation、precipice、precipitous 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one motion: something goes over an edge. It happens in a beaker as a solid, in a solution as a settling, in history as a sudden event, in a schedule as haste, in grammar as an adjective, a noun and finally as falling weather.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项保留同一个动作：某物越过边缘。它在烧杯里成为固体，在溶液里成为沉降，在历史中成为突发事件，在日程上成为加速，在语法上成为形容词与名词，最后成为落下的天气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a substance held in suspension suddenly crosses a threshold and falls out.
core.cn: 核心意象：悬浮着的物质忽然越过一个门槛，掉了出来。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY, ACTIVE AND PASSIVE: an agent can throw the solid down, or the solid can fall by itself.
branches.cn: 化学的主动与被动：可以由试剂把固体抛下，也可以由固体自己落下。

branches.en: TIME PUSHED FORWARD: an event is brought into the present, either abruptly or merely faster.
branches.cn: 时间被向前推：事件被拉进现在，或骤然发生，或只是更快。

branches.en: CHARACTER: a mind that dives before looking is called precipitate.
branches.cn: 性格：还没看清就往下扎的心智，被叫作 precipitate。

branches.en: PRODUCT: what has fallen out is a deposit with a name of its own.
branches.cn: 产物：落出来的东西是一个有自己名字的沉淀物。

branches.en: THE LITERAL FALL: a body thrown from a height, and water thrown down by the sky.
branches.cn: 字面坠落：被从高处抛下的身体，以及被天空抛下的水。

intro.en: Precipitate carries the Latin pieces prae- and capit-. English then adds -ation, -ous, -ice, -ant and -or to build the rest of the family.
intro.cn: precipitate 带着拉丁构件 prae- 与 capit-。英语再加 -ation、-ous、-ice、-ant、-or 构成其余词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries are recorded forms of the family; the base noun caput is given because it explains why 'headlong' is inside every derivative.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁条目是该词族有记录的形式；列出基础名词 caput，是因为它解释了为什么每个派生词里都藏着「头朝下」。

items.meaning: the process of falling, or of a solid forming
items.meaningCN: 降落的过程；固体析出的过程（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Precipitation removes the metal from the wastewater.
items.exampleCN: 沉淀法把金属从废水中去除。

items.meaningCN: 极陡的；也有仓促义（-ous 表示「充满……」）
items.example: The trail turned precipitous after the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 过了山脊之后，小路变得陡峭。

items.meaning: a cliff face or a dangerous brink
items.example: One more step would take him over the precipice.
items.exampleCN: 再走一步他就会跌下悬崖。

items.meaning: a reagent that makes a solid settle out
items.meaningCN: 使固体沉降的沉淀剂（-ant 表示施动者）
items.example: Alum is a common precipitant in water treatment.
items.exampleCN: 明矾是水处理中常见的沉淀剂。

items.meaning: an apparatus that collects particles from a gas
items.meaningCN: 从气体中捕集颗粒的器具（-or 表示器具）
items.example: The precipitator removes dust from the smokestack.
items.exampleCN: 除尘器把烟囱里的粉尘除掉。

items.meaning: to separate from a solution and settle
items.meaningCN: 从溶液中析出并沉降（out 表示「出来」）
items.example: The crystals precipitate out when the solution cools.
items.exampleCN: 溶液冷却时晶体会析出。

items.meaning: a reaction whose product is an insoluble solid
items.meaningCN: 产物为不溶固体的沉淀反应
items.example: A precipitation reaction produced the blue solid.
items.exampleCN: 一个沉淀反应生成了蓝色固体。

items.meaningCN: 仓促地；鲁莽地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: He left precipitately before the vote.

latinEntries.meaning: to throw down headlong; to hasten

latinEntries.meaningCN: 头朝下的；陡峭的；鲁莽的

definition_zh: 降水；降水量；（化学）沉淀；沉淀物；仓促
definition_en: water that falls from clouds as rain, snow, hail or sleet, or a solid that forms out of a solution
core_image: 云里的小水滴越聚越多，云托不住，一齐落向地面
scene: 山脊上的雨量筒一夜之间就积满了水。Overnight precipitation filled the rain gauge on the ridge.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「从云中落到地面的水」（第 1 个义项：雨、雪、冰雹等从天而降的水）；句意为一夜之间的降水装满了山脊上的雨量筒。

pos.zh: 降水；降水量；（化学）沉淀；沉淀物；仓促

collocations.phrase: precipitation in the form of snow
collocations.zh: 以降雪形式出现的降水

derivatives.zh: 使沉淀；促成 / 沉淀物 / 仓促的

senses.title: Water falling from clouds
senses.definition: water that falls from the atmosphere to the ground
senses.definitionCN: 从大气降落到地面的水
senses.example: Overnight precipitation filled the rain gauge on the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一夜之间的降水装满了山脊上的雨量筒。
senses.why: The Latin verb means 'to throw headlong'; the meteorologists' noun keeps that downward motion and applies it to water leaving the sky.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「头朝下抛落」；气象学的名词保留了这个向下动作，只是把落下的东西换成了离开天空的水。

senses.title: Snow, hail or sleet as forms of fall
senses.titleCN: 雪、冰雹、雨夹雪等降落形式
senses.definition: any form in which water falls, whether liquid or frozen
senses.definitionCN: 水降落的任何一种形态，无论液态还是冻结
senses.example: Winter precipitation in the mountains usually arrives as snow.
senses.exampleCN: 山区的冬季降水通常以雪的形式到来。
senses.why: Rain is only the commonest case; the word covers the whole class, so frozen forms count as the same event.
senses.whyCN: 雨只是最常见的一种；这个词覆盖整个类别，所以冻结形态也算同一种事件。

senses.title: The measured total
senses.definition: the amount of water that has fallen, usually measured in millimetres or inches
senses.definitionCN: 已经落下的水量，通常以毫米或英寸计
senses.example: The desert receives less than ten inches of precipitation a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沙漠每年降水不足十英寸。
senses.why: Once rain is caught in a gauge, the event turns into a quantity, and the same noun names the number.
senses.whyCN: 一旦雨被雨量筒接住，事件就变成了数量，同一个名词也就用来指这个数字。

senses.title: A solid forming in a solution
senses.definition: in chemistry, the process by which a dissolved substance becomes a solid
senses.definitionCN: 化学中指溶解的物质变成固体的过程
senses.example: Adding the salt caused precipitation of the dissolved silver.
senses.exampleCN: 加入这种盐使溶解的银发生了沉淀。
senses.why: A substance that was spread through a liquid suddenly stops being dissolved; it 'throws itself down' as a solid, the same image as rain leaving a cloud.
senses.whyCN: 原本分散在液体里的物质忽然不再溶解，以固体的形态「把自己抛下来」，与雨离开云是同一个意象。

senses.title: The solid that comes out
senses.definition: the solid material produced by that chemical process
senses.definitionCN: 该化学过程产生的固体物质
senses.example: The white precipitation was filtered off and dried.
senses.exampleCN: 白色沉淀物被滤出并烘干。
senses.why: English uses the same word for the process and for its product, because the product is simply the process seen as a finished thing.
senses.whyCN: 英语用同一个词既指过程也指产物，因为产物就是过程完成后被看作一个东西。

senses.title: A sudden onset of events
senses.definition: the act of making something happen suddenly or too soon
senses.definitionCN: 使某事突然或过早发生
senses.example: The report warns against precipitation of a trade war.
senses.exampleCN: 报告警告不要贸然引发贸易战。
senses.why: The old sense 'throwing headlong' moved from bodies to events: a crisis that is precipitated falls on people all at once.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「头朝下抛落」从身体移到了事件：被促成的危机一下子砸到人头上。

senses.title: Haste or rashness
senses.definition: the quality of acting too quickly, without enough thought
senses.definitionCN: 行动过快、思虑不足的性质
senses.example: He acted with precipitation and lost the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 他行事仓促，丢掉了那份合同。
senses.why: Someone who rushes is 'falling headlong' in behaviour rather than in body, so the metaphor becomes a judgement of character.
senses.whyCN: 匆忙的人是行为上「头朝下栽」，而非身体上，于是这个比喻变成对人的评价。

senses.title: The meteorological process
senses.definition: the whole process by which water vapour condenses and falls
senses.definitionCN: 水汽凝结并落下的整个过程
senses.example: Cold air over the lake increases precipitation along the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 湖面上的冷空气增加了沿岸的降水。
senses.why: This sense names the mechanism rather than the result, the same event viewed as a chain of steps.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项指机制而不是结果，是同一事件被看作一串步骤。

intro.en: Every sense goes back to one Latin verb meaning 'to throw headlong'. The word entered English through borrowed Latin, not through inheritance. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 所有义项都回到同一个拉丁动词，意为「头朝下抛落」。这个词经拉丁语借入英语，而非本土传承。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Latin praecipitatio meant 'a falling headlong' or 'haste', formed from praecipitare 'to throw down headlong'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 praecipitatio 意为「头朝下坠落」或「仓促」，由 praecipitare「头朝下抛落」构成。

items.en: The verb joins prae- 'before, forth' with caput 'head' (stem capit-). The picture is someone diving forward, head first.
items.cn: 这个动词由 prae-「在前、向前」与 caput「头」（词干 capit-）组成。画面是一个人向前、头朝下地栽下去。

items.en: Alchemical and medical Latin used praecipitatio for a substance settling out of a liquid, and English writers borrowed this technical sense.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语中的炼金术与医学用语用 praecipitatio 指物质从液体中沉降出来，英语作者借入了这一技术义。

items.en: Meteorologists applied the same noun to rain and snow falling from clouds, the modern everyday sense.
items.cn: 十七世纪的气象写作者把同一个名词用到从云中落下的雨雪上，形成现代日常义。

items.en: Chemistry standardized precipitation for the formation of a solid, and climate science made it the standard word for measured rainfall and snowfall totals.
items.cn: 十九至二十世纪，化学把 precipitation 固定为固体析出的术语，气候科学则用它作为雨雪总量的标准词。

note.en: Group one holds longer words that share the -pitation shape; group two holds the everyday weather words it covers.
note.cn: 第一组是与该词共享 -pitation 词形的长词；第二组是它所涵盖的日常天气词。

entries.definition: Taking part in an activity. It comes from Latin particeps 'sharing', and the -cip- here is from capere 'to take', a different family.
entries.definitionCN: 参与某项活动。源自拉丁语 particeps「分享」，其中的 -cip- 出自 capere「拿取」，属另一词族。

entries.definition: The act of noticing or understanding something. It comes from percipere 'to seize wholly', not from praecipitare.
entries.definitionCN: 察觉或理解某事的行为。源自 percipere「完全抓住」，并非出自 praecipitare。

entries.definition: The act of getting something ready. The base is parare 'to make ready', so the resemblance is only in length and rhythm.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物准备好的行为。词基是 parare「准备」，相似之处只在词长与节奏。

entries.definition: Rain measured over a period; it excludes snow and hail, while precipitation includes every form.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间内测得的雨量；它不包括雪和冰雹，而 precipitation 包含一切形态。

entries.definition: Snow that falls, or its measured amount; it is one member of the precipitation class.
entries.definitionCN: 落下的雪或其测定量；它是降水这一大类中的一种。

entries.definition: The change from vapour to liquid that must happen before precipitation; it names the step, not the fall.
entries.definitionCN: 降水发生前必须完成的水汽变液体；它指这一步，而不是落下。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin pieces, real chemistry terms, no invented stories.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：使用真实的拉丁构件与化学术语，不编故事。

normal.en: pre- 'before' + capit- 'head' + -ation: something that goes head first out of the sky or out of a solution.
normal.cn: pre-「在前」+ capit-「头」+ -ation：从天空或溶液里「头朝下」出来的东西。

normal.en: precipitation and precipitate share one root; precipitation is the process, precipitate is the solid or the verb.
normal.cn: precipitation 与 precipitate 共享一个词根：前者是过程，后者是固体或动词。

normal.en: precipitous 'steep' keeps the same image: a cliff where one false step sends you head first.
normal.cn: precipitous「陡峭的」保留同一意象：在悬崖上一步踏错就会头朝下栽下去。

normal.en: acid precipitation is the technical name behind the everyday term acid rain.
normal.cn: acid precipitation 是日常说法 acid rain（酸雨）背后的技术名称。

normal.en: The gauge phrase precipitation total pairs the event with its number, which is why the noun can mean both.
normal.cn: precipitation total 这一搭配把事件与数字配在一起，这正是该名词能同时指两者的原因。

abstract.en: Abstractly, precipitation is anything that leaves a floating state and goes down: water leaving a cloud, a solid leaving a solution, a crisis leaving the future and landing in the present.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，precipitation 是任何离开悬浮状态而向下落的东西：水离开云，固体离开溶液，危机离开未来而落到眼前。

abstract.en: The direction is always downward, and the agent is always something that can no longer stay suspended.
abstract.cn: 方向永远是向下，主体永远是那个再也悬浮不住的东西。

abstract.en: So the weather sense and the chemistry sense are one geometry: a ceiling gives way, and what was held falls.
abstract.cn: 所以天气义与化学义是同一个几何：顶托不住了，原本被托住的东西就落下来。

examples.en: The station records precipitation every morning at eight.
examples.cn: 该站每天早上八点记录降水量。

examples.en: Calcium carbonate precipitation sealed the cracks in the cave floor.
examples.cn: 碳酸钙沉淀把洞底的裂缝封住了。

examples.en: A sudden precipitation of events left the negotiators no time to consult.
examples.cn: 事态的骤然爆发让谈判者来不及磋商。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「泼湿皮特」：天上泼下水，把皮特浇湿 → precipitation 降水

root: 拉丁语 praecipitatio「头朝下坠落」← praecipitare「抛落」，由 prae-「向前」+ caput「头」构成；与 precipice、precipitous 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one downward motion. Water falls from a cloud, is counted in a gauge, takes frozen forms, then the same motion appears in a beaker as a solid, in public life as a sudden event, and in character as haste.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个向下动作。水从云里落下，被雨量筒计量，呈现冻结形态；随后同一动作出现在烧杯里成为固体，在公共生活中成为突发事件，在性格上成为仓促。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something held up by a ceiling suddenly gives way and falls head first.
core.cn: 核心意象：被一层顶托住的东西忽然失去支撑，头朝下坠落。

branches.en: WHAT FALLS: liquid rain and frozen snow or hail are one class of falling water.
branches.cn: 落下之物：液态的雨与冻结的雪、冰雹都属同一类落下的水。

branches.en: HOW MUCH: a gauge turns the event into millimetres and inches.
branches.cn: 落了多少：雨量筒把事件变成毫米与英寸。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: a dissolved substance leaves the liquid as a solid, and the solid takes the same name.
branches.cn: 化学：溶解的物质离开液体成为固体，这个固体也用同一个名称。

branches.en: HUMAN TIME: an event falls on people too soon, and the person who causes it is judged hasty.
branches.cn: 人的时间：事件过早砸到人身上，促成它的人则被评判为仓促。

branches.en: MECHANISM: meteorology names the whole condensation-and-fall chain.
branches.cn: 机制：气象学用这个词命名凝结到落下的整条链条。

intro.en: The family is built from Latin prae- plus caput. English adds -ation for the process, -ous for the steep version, and -or for an instrument.
intro.cn: 这个词族由拉丁 prae- 加 caput 构成。英语加 -ation 表示过程，加 -ous 表示陡峭，加 -or 表示器具。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries below are the recorded ancestors and relatives of the family; they are listed as Latin, not as modern English words.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁条目是该词族有记录的祖先与亲属；它们按拉丁语列出，而不是现代英语词。

items.meaning: to cause a solid to form; the solid itself; hasty
items.meaningCN: 使固体析出；析出的固体；仓促的
items.example: The reagent precipitates the metal as a salt.
items.exampleCN: 试剂使金属以盐的形式沉淀出来。

items.meaning: extremely steep, like a cliff that drops away
items.meaningCN: 陡峭的，像骤然下落的悬崖（-ous 表示「充满……」）
items.example: A precipitous path led down to the shore.
items.exampleCN: 一条陡峭的小路通向岸边。

items.meaning: a very steep cliff or a dangerous situation
items.example: The goats stood at the edge of the precipice.

items.meaning: a substance that causes another substance to precipitate
items.meaningCN: 沉淀剂（-ant 表示施动者）
items.example: Add the precipitant slowly and stir.
items.exampleCN: 缓慢加入沉淀剂并搅拌。

items.meaning: a device that removes particles from a gas by electrical attraction
items.meaningCN: 静电除尘器；沉淀器（-or 表示器具）
items.example: The electrostatic precipitator catches the fly ash.

items.meaning: a chemical reaction that produces an insoluble solid
items.meaningCN: 沉淀反应（生成不溶固体的化学反应）
items.example: The lab demonstrates a precipitation reaction with silver nitrate.
items.exampleCN: 实验用硝酸银演示一个沉淀反应。

items.meaning: rain or snow made acidic by dissolved pollutants
items.meaningCN: 酸性降水；酸雨（因溶解污染物而呈酸性的雨雪）
items.example: Acid precipitation has damaged the lakes.
items.exampleCN: 酸性降水已经损害了这些湖泊。

items.meaning: the act or factor that causes something to happen or settle
items.meaningCN: 促成……的；正在沉淀的（-ing 分词形式）
items.example: A poor harvest was the precipitating cause of the revolt.
items.exampleCN: 歉收是这场起义的直接诱因。

latinEntries.meaning: to throw down headlong; to hasten

latinEntries.meaningCN: 头朝下的；陡峭的；鲁莽的

definition_zh: 精确的；准确的；明确的；严谨的；恰好的
definition_en: exact and accurate in detail; clearly defined and not approximate; careful about details
core_image: 一刀切下去，边缘干净，不多不少
scene: 这台仪器能把温度测到十分之一个刻度。The instrument can measure temperature to a precise tenth of a degree.
sceneCN: 这里 precise 是「精确到很小单位」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这台仪器能把温度测量到十分之一度的精确度。场景要点：刻度细、读数明确、没有模糊区间；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 精确的；准确的；明确的；严谨的

senses.title: Exact in measurement
senses.titleCN: 精确的：读数细到很小一格
senses.definition: exact and accurate, with details measured or stated to a fine degree
senses.definitionCN: 精确而准确，细节被测量或陈述到很细的程度
senses.example: The instrument can measure temperature to a precise tenth of a degree.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器能把温度测量到十分之一度的精确度。
senses.why: Latin praecidere means to cut off. A precise measurement is one cut cleanly, with no ragged margin of doubt.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praecidere 意为“切掉”。精确的测量就是切得干净，边缘没有参差的疑问。

senses.title: Clearly defined and distinct
senses.definition: clearly stated or defined, so that there is no ambiguity
senses.definitionCN: 陈述或界定清楚，因而没有歧义
senses.example: The contract gives a precise definition of the delivery date.
senses.exampleCN: 合同对交付日期给出了明确的定义。
senses.why: If the edges are cut cleanly, the shape is unambiguous. A precise definition has no fuzzy border where other things could slip in.
senses.whyCN: 边缘切得干净，形状就不含糊。明确的定义没有模糊的边界，别的东西无从混入。

senses.title: Careful about small details
senses.titleCN: 严谨的：在小处也不放过
senses.definition: careful and exact in doing or describing something, paying attention to small details
senses.definitionCN: 在做或描述某事时仔细准确，注意细小之处
senses.example: She is precise about the order of the steps.
senses.exampleCN: 她对步骤的先后十分严谨。
senses.why: The cut-clean image becomes a habit of mind: refusing to let any detail stay rough.
senses.whyCN: “切得干净”的画面变成一种思维习惯：不允许任何细节保持粗糙。

senses.title: Strict about rules or standards
senses.titleCN: 讲究的：按规矩来，不将就
senses.definition: strict and particular about how things are done, often in matters of form
senses.definitionCN: 对做事方式严格挑剔，常指形式与礼数方面
senses.example: He was precise in his dress and punctual to the minute.
senses.exampleCN: 他衣着讲究，并且准时到分钟。
senses.why: A person who cuts every edge cleanly can become a person who insists on exact form. The trait shifts from result to temperament.
senses.whyCN: 一个把每条边都切干净的人，可能变成坚持确切形式的人。这个特征从结果转到了性情。

senses.title: Emphatic: the very same
senses.definition: used to emphasize that a particular thing or moment is exactly the one meant
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调所说的正是那一个事物或那一刻
senses.example: At that precise moment, the lights went out.
senses.exampleCN: 正是在那一刻，灯灭了。
senses.why: An exact point has no width. Using precise here says the moment cannot be widened into a general period.
senses.whyCN: 一个精确的点没有宽度。这里用 precise，是说那一刻无法被放宽成一段笼统的时期。

senses.title: Technical: high precision
senses.titleCN: 精密的：仪器能做到极细刻度
senses.definition: of an instrument or method, able to produce very exact results
senses.definitionCN: 指仪器或方法能给出非常精确的结果
senses.example: Precise instruments are required for this experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验需要精密的仪器。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to the tool that makes the clean cut. Precision becomes a property of the instrument, not only of the number.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词贴到了做出干净切割的工具上。精确性成了仪器的属性，而不只是数字的属性。

senses.title: Discourse: to be exact
senses.definition: in the phrase to be precise, used to correct or narrow what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 在 to be precise 这一短语中，用来修正或收窄刚才说过的话
senses.example: He arrived late, at ten past eight, to be precise.
senses.exampleCN: 他到得晚了，确切地说是八点十分。
senses.why: The speaker performs the cutting in speech: trimming a rough statement down to its exact edge.
senses.whyCN: 说话人在言语里执行这一刀：把粗略的说法修到确切的边缘。

senses.title: Neatly executed in movement or art
senses.titleCN: 动作精准：每一笔每一动都不含糊
senses.definition: performed with exact control, as in dance, surgery, or drawing
senses.definitionCN: 以精确的控制完成，如舞蹈、手术或绘画中的动作
senses.example: The dancer's precise movements made the whole phrase look effortless.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者精准的动作让整个乐句显得毫不费力。
senses.why: The body can cut cleanly too. Precision in movement is the same refusal of slack, expressed in muscle.
senses.whyCN: 身体也能切得干净。动作的精准是同一种对松弛的拒绝，只是用肌肉表达出来。

intro.en: Precise comes from a Latin participle meaning cut off. The path from 'cut short' to 'exact' is the story of a metaphor that became a standard.
intro.cn: precise 来自一个意为“被切掉”的拉丁分词。从“切短”到“精确”的路径，是一个比喻变成标准的历程。

items.en: Prae meant 'before, in front'. Here it intensifies rather than marks time: the cutting is done right at the front edge.
items.cn: prae 意为“在前”。这里它起加强作用而非标时间：这一刀正切在前沿上。

items.en: Caedere meant 'to cut, to strike'. English gets scissors, decide, concise, and circumcise from this family.
items.cn: caedere 意为“切、砍”。英语的 scissors、decide、concise、circumcise 都出自这个词族。

items.en: Praecidere meant 'to cut off, to cut short'. It described trimming something down to a clean limit.
items.cn: praecidere 意为“切掉、切短”。它描述把某物修到干净的界限。

items.en: The past participle praecisus meant 'cut off, shortened'. It is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.cn: 过去分词 praecisus 意为“被切掉的、被缩短的”。它是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.en: French used précis for 'cut short, concise, exact'. English borrowed the form in the 16th century.
items.cn: 法语用 précis 表示“切短的、简洁的、确切的”。英语在 16 世纪借入这个词形。

items.en: The sense moves from 'cut short' to 'definite' and then to 'accurate to a fine degree'. Modern usage applies it to numbers, definitions, instruments, people, and moments.
items.cn: 词义从“切短”转到“确定”，再转到“精确到很细的程度”。现代用法把它用于数字、定义、仪器、人以及时刻。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for cutting. The second group collects words for accuracy and exactness.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“切”的动词。第二组收表示准确与确切的词。

entries.definition: the quality of being exact, or the degree of exactness. It is the noun built on precise.
entries.definitionCN: 精确的性质，或精确的程度。它是建立在 precise 之上的名词。

entries.definition: exactly, or used to confirm a statement. Precisely can answer a question with a firm yes.
entries.definitionCN: 精确地，或用于确认某陈述。precisely 可以以干脆的“正是”来回答提问。

entries.definition: brief and clear. Con- 'together' plus caedere 'cut': cut down to essentials.
entries.definitionCN: 简短而清楚。con-“一起”加 caedere“切”：切到只剩要点。

entries.definition: to settle a question. De- 'off' plus caedere 'cut': cut off alternatives until one remains.
entries.definitionCN: 把问题定下来。de-“去掉”加 caedere“切”：切掉其他选项，直到只剩一个。

entries.definition: correct in every detail. Exact stresses correctness; precise stresses fine definition and care.
entries.definitionCN: 每个细节都正确。exact 强调正确；precise 强调界定细密与讲究。

entries.definition: correct and free from error. Accurate is about truth to fact; precise is about narrowness of specification.
entries.definitionCN: 正确且无错误。accurate 关乎与事实相符；precise 关乎规格的窄细。

entries.definition: clearly identified rather than general. Specific names the thing; precise describes how finely it is defined.
entries.definitionCN: 明确指出的，而非笼统的。specific 指名的是哪一个；precise 描述界定得多细。

entries.definition: showing great attention to detail. Meticulous fits sense 03 and stresses care rather than measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 对细节极为注意。meticulous 对应第 3 义项，强调用心而非测量。

entries.definition: clear and not uncertain. Definite fits sense 02 and is close to the 'cut clean' image.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而不含糊。definite 对应第 2 义项，贴近“切得干净”的画面。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the clean cut, the narrow definition, the meticulous person, the exact instant, and the phrase to be precise.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：干净的一刀、窄而清楚的定义、一丝不苟的人、正好的那一刻、以及 to be precise 这句话。

normal.en: Precise comes from a verb meaning to cut off. Picture a knife trimming away every loose edge.
normal.cn: precise 来自意为“切掉”的动词。想象一把刀把每一条松散的边都修掉。

normal.en: A precise definition has a clean border: nothing else can slip in.
normal.cn: 明确的定义有一条干净的边界：别的东西混不进来。

normal.en: Precise instruments are the ones whose readings do not wobble.
normal.cn: 精密的仪器，就是读数不会晃的那种。

normal.en: At that precise moment means the moment has no width; you cannot widen it into an afternoon.
normal.cn: at that precise moment 意为那一刻没有宽度，你不能把它放宽成一个下午。

normal.en: To be precise is to take the rough sentence and trim it to its exact edge.
normal.cn: to be precise 就是把粗糙的句子修到确切的边缘。

abstract.en: Precision is a relation between a statement and a tolerance, not a property of the world by itself.
abstract.cn: 精确是陈述与容许误差之间的关系，不是世界本身的属性。

abstract.en: Every precise definition is also an exclusion: to say exactly what it is, is to say what it is not.
abstract.cn: 每个明确的定义同时也是一次排除：说清它是什么，就是说清它不是什么。

abstract.en: The same cut that makes a thing exact can make it narrow; precision always trades scope for edge.
abstract.cn: 使事物精确的那一刀，也可能使它变窄；精确总是用范围换取边缘。

examples.en: The instructions were precise enough that a beginner could follow them.
examples.cn: 这些指示足够精确，初学者也能照着做。

examples.en: To be precise, the meeting lasted forty-two minutes.
examples.cn: 确切地说，会议持续了四十二分钟。

examples.en: Her precise handwriting filled the margins without a single correction.
examples.cn: 她精准的字迹填满了页边，没有一处涂改。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞赛斯”——普瑞在赛前把秒表按到千分之一秒，就是 precise（精确的）

root: 拉丁语 praecidere“切掉、切短”（prae“在前”+ caedere“切”）的过去分词 praecisus → 法语 précis → 英语 precise（16 世纪）；与 concise、decide、scissors 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a clean cut. A clean cut gives exact numbers, unambiguous definitions, meticulous habits, and instruments that do not wobble. The emphatic use fixes one instant, and to be precise performs the same trimming in speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是干净的一刀。干净的一刀给出精确的数字、不含糊的定义、一丝不苟的习惯，以及不晃的仪器。强调用法固定住某一刻，而 to be precise 是在言语里执行同一番修边。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade trimming an edge until nothing rough is left.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀刃修边，直到不剩一点毛糙。

branches.en: MEASURE: exact readings and the instruments that produce them.
branches.cn: 测量：精确的读数，以及产生这些读数的仪器。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: a definition with a clean edge, and a moment with no width.
branches.cn: 边界：边缘干净的定义，以及没有宽度的时刻。

branches.en: TEMPERAMENT: the meticulous person and the person strict about form.
branches.cn: 性情：一丝不苟的人，以及讲究形式的人。

branches.en: SPEECH: trimming a rough statement down to the exact word.
branches.cn: 言语：把粗略的说法修到确切的字眼。

branches.en: MOVEMENT: the same clean edge performed by the body.
branches.cn: 动作：由身体执行的同一种干净边缘。

intro.en: Precise is one participle from the cut family. The same verb, with different prefixes, gives concise, decide, and scissors.
intro.cn: precise 是“切”词族里的一个分词。同一个动词配上不同前缀，给出 concise、decide、scissors。

latinIntro.en: Latin praecisus reached English through French précis, which is why the English form lacks the Latin -us ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 praecisus 经法语 précis 到达英语，所以英语形式没有拉丁的 -us 词尾。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
表示状态或性质的名词后缀

definition_zh: 精确；精密度；精确性；（仪器、测量的）精度；有效数字位数；（加工）公差
definition_en: the quality of being exact, especially the fineness of a measurement or the closeness of repeated readings to one another
core_image: 一把薄刃把多余的部分削掉，只留下真正要的那一点
scene: 实验室的台面上摆着一支滴定管、一本记录册和一台电子天平，同一份样品被反复称了五回。The precision of the balance showed in five readings that differed by less than a milligram.
sceneCN: 这里 precision 指「统计意义上的重复一致性」（第 2 个义项：重复测量的一致程度）；句意：这台天平的精密度体现在五次读数相差不到一毫克。图中可辨识物件：滴定管、记录册、电子天平、样品瓶；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 精确；精密度；精度；精确性

senses.title: The fineness of a stated measurement
senses.titleCN: 测量值本身的精细程度
senses.definition: the degree to which a stated measurement is divided into fine enough steps for two nearby values to be told apart
senses.definitionCN: 一个测量值被细分到多细的程度，即能否把两个接近的值区分开
senses.example: The precision of the reading was limited by the smallest mark on the ruler.
senses.exampleCN: 这个读数的精度受限于尺子上最小的那道刻度。
senses.why: Praecisio is a cutting off, and a finely stated measurement is one cut into narrow slices.
senses.whyCN: praecisio 本义是切去，精细报出的测量值就是把量切成一薄片一薄片。

senses.title: Repeatability across repeated measurements
senses.definition: in statistics, the closeness of repeated measurements to one another, whether or not they sit near the true value
senses.definitionCN: 统计上多次测量彼此接近的程度，与它们是否靠近真值无关
senses.example: The five runs showed high precision even when the average was slightly off.
senses.exampleCN: 五次运行即使平均值略有偏差，重复精密度依然很高。
senses.why: Statistics separates the scatter among repeats, called precision, from the distance to the truth, called accuracy.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把重复测量的分散程度称为精密度，把与真值的距离称为准确度，两者分开。

senses.title: The smallest step an instrument can show
senses.definition: the smallest change in a quantity that an instrument can register, display or resolve
senses.definitionCN: 仪器能够记录、显示或分辨的最小变化量
senses.example: The instrument's precision reaches one part in a million.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器的精度达到百万分之一。
senses.why: An instrument whose scale is cut more finely can separate values that a coarse one merges.
senses.whyCN: 刻度切得更细的仪器，能把粗仪器混在一起的值分开。

senses.title: Exactness in wording
senses.definition: careful exactness in the choice of words, so that a statement admits only one reading
senses.definitionCN: 用词上的细致准确，使一句话只容许一种读法
senses.example: She described the procedure with the precision of a manual.
senses.exampleCN: 她像操作手册一样精确地描述了步骤。
senses.why: Latin praecisio also meant brevity of speech, where every surplus word has been cut away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praecisio 也指言辞简省，即把多余的词都切掉。

senses.title: Targeted action on a small site
senses.titleCN: 精准农业与精准医疗的定点干预
senses.definition: an approach that directs water, treatment or medicine only to the exact field, place or patient that needs it
senses.definitionCN: 只把水、处理或药物投到确切需要的田块、地点或病人身上的做法
senses.example: Precision irrigation delivers water to the driest rows alone.
senses.exampleCN: 精准灌溉只把水送到最干的那几垄。
senses.why: The modern compounds keep the old image of a cut made exactly where it is wanted.
senses.whyCN: 现代复合词保留了老意象：只在需要的地方下刀。

senses.title: The number of reliable digits
senses.definition: the count of digits in a reported value that carry real information about how finely it is known
senses.definitionCN: 一个报告值中携带真实精细信息的数字位数
senses.example: Report the mean to four digits of precision.
senses.exampleCN: 把平均值报到四位有效数字。
senses.why: Digits past the reliable cut are noise, so counting the trustworthy digits states the precision.
senses.whyCN: 可靠切点之后的位只是噪声，数出可信位数就是在说明精度。

senses.title: Machining to a very small tolerance
senses.titleCN: 机械加工的公差与精度
senses.definition: the closeness with which a machined part matches its specified size, measured in very small units
senses.definitionCN: 加工件与规定尺寸吻合的紧密程度，以极小的单位计量
senses.example: The shop grinds bearings to a precision of two microns.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把轴承磨到两微米的精度。
senses.why: In a machine shop the abstract fineness becomes metal cut away until the part fits.
senses.whyCN: 在机加工车间，抽象的精细变成被切掉的金属，直到零件合适。

senses.title: Strict exactness in legal or formal form
senses.titleCN: 法律或形式上的严格精确
senses.definition: the strict following of exact wording or procedure, where no looseness or paraphrase is permitted
senses.definitionCN: 严格遵循确切的措辞或程序，不允许任何松动或改写
senses.example: The clause was drafted with precision to close every loophole.
senses.exampleCN: 这一条款起草得十分精确，堵住了每个漏洞。
senses.why: A legal cut must fall on exactly the right word, which is the original image applied to text.
senses.whyCN: 法律之刀必须落在确切的字上，正是原意象用在文本上。

intro.en: Precision comes from Latin praecisio 'a cutting off', a noun of action from praecidere 'to cut short', built on prae- 'in front' plus caedere 'to cut'. French carried the word into English in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: precision 出自拉丁 praecisio「切去」，是 praecidere「切短」的动作名词，由 prae-「在前」加 caedere「切」构成。英语十六世纪经法语引入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Caedere meant 'to cut, to strike down'; it also underlies incision, excise and decision, each of which turns on a cut.
items.cn: caedere 意为「切、砍倒」，也构成 incision、excise 与 decision，这几个词都围绕「切」展开。

items.en: Prae- 'in front' plus caedere made praecidere 'to cut off in front, to shorten'; a speech that was praecisus had its surplus trimmed away.
items.cn: prae-「在前」加 caedere 构成 praecidere「切去前面、截短」；被称作 praecisus 的言辞就是把多余部分削掉了。

items.en: Praecisio named the act of cutting off and also brevity of style, so the notion of fine trimming sits inside both senses.
items.cn: praecisio 既指切去的动作，也指文风的简省，因此「削到恰好」的观念同时存在于这两层。

items.en: Middle French precision brought the word into English, first for concise speech and only later for exact measurement.
items.cn: 中古法语 precision 把这个词带进英语，先用于简练的言辞，较晚才用于精确测量。

items.en: Nineteenth-century science and manufacturing applied the word to instrument scales and machined parts, which produced the modern technical senses.
items.cn: 十九世纪的科学与制造业把这个词用到仪器刻度和加工零件上，现代技术义项由此形成。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the direct source is Latin praecisio, attested in the classical language, so the word itself is not in doubt; only the exact year of its first English use is not recorded. The usual route is through French, while a direct Latin borrowing is also argued; no single route is imposed here.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：直接来源是有据可查的拉丁语 praecisio，词本身并不存疑；只是英语最早用例的具体年份没有记录。通常认为经法语传入，也有直接借自拉丁语的说法；此处不强行选定单一传入路径。

note.en: Group one is the same Latin family seen through its adjective, adverb and negative forms; group two holds the measuring partners that share the field but answer a different question.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁词族在形容词、副词与否定形式上的样子；第二组是同处测量领域的伙伴词，但它们回答的是另一个问题。

entries.definition: Giving exact details with nothing vague; it describes the thing or the person, while precision names the quality itself.
entries.definitionCN: 给出确切细节、毫不含糊；它形容事物或人，而 precision 是这种性质本身。

entries.definition: In an exact way, or used as an emphatic 'exactly'; it modifies an action rather than naming a measured degree.
entries.definitionCN: 以确切的方式，或用作加强语气的「正是」；它修饰动作，不指一个测得的程度。

entries.definition: Lack of exactness, formed with the negative prefix im-; it is the direct opposite of precision in every sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不精确，由否定前缀 im- 构成；在各义项上都是 precision 的反面。

entries.definition: A less common synonym for precision, stressing the manner of being exact rather than a measured degree of fineness.
entries.definitionCN: precision 的罕用同义词，强调一丝不苟的作风，而非测得的精细程度。

entries.definition: How near a measurement lies to the true value; a rifle can be accurate while its shots are widely spread.
entries.definitionCN: 测量值与真值的接近程度；一支枪可以很准确，但弹着点散布很广。

entries.definition: The state of being wholly correct, often said of a figure or a copy rather than of a spread of repeats.
entries.definitionCN: 完全正确的状态，常用于数字或副本，而不是重复测量的散布。

entries.definition: The smallest interval an instrument or an image can distinguish; it is the hardware side of precision.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器或图像能分辨的最小间隔；它是精密度在硬件上的表现。

entries.definition: The range of variation a specification allows; precision is the aim, tolerance is the slack accepted around it.
entries.definitionCN: 规格允许的变动范围；precision 是瞄准的目标，tolerance 是允许的松量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin cut, the fine scale and the fixed phrases that keep the word technical.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语的「切」、细密的刻度，以及把这个词固定在技术语境里的搭配。

normal.en: Prae- 'before' plus caedere 'to cut': trim off the surplus.
normal.cn: prae-「在前」加 caedere「切」：把多余的部分削掉。

normal.en: A fine scale cuts a quantity into narrow slices.
normal.cn: 细密的刻度把一个量切成一薄片一薄片。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: precision measurement, precision instrument, precision farming.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：精密测量、精密仪器、精准农业。

normal.en: Statistics keeps precision for repeats and accuracy for the true value.
normal.cn: 统计学用「精密度」说重复，用「准确度」说真值。

normal.en: In a machine shop precision is measured in microns.
normal.cn: 在机加工车间，精度以微米计。

abstract.en: Picture a blade shaving a hair's width off a metal block.
abstract.cn: 想象刀刃从金属块上削下一根头发那么薄的一层。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler whose marks sit closer together than a fingernail.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子，刻度线比指甲还窄。

abstract.en: Picture five arrows in one tight cluster, though none of them near the bullseye.
abstract.cn: 想象五支箭扎在同一小簇里，却都不靠近靶心。

examples.en: The survey reported its margin with more precision than the sample size deserved.
examples.cn: 这项调查报出的误差范围，比它的样本量所能支撑的更为精细。

examples.en: Precision alone does not make a scale trustworthy if it was zeroed wrongly.
examples.cn: 如果零点调错了，光有精密度并不能让一台秤可信。

examples.en: Precision medicine matches a drug to the genetic profile of one patient.
examples.cn: 精准医疗把药物匹配到某一位病人的基因特征上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pre（在前）+ cise（切）」——把多余的部分切掉，留下的就是精确

root: 拉丁 praecisio「切去」= praecidere（prae-「在前」+ caedere「切」）的动作名词。同族词有 precise、precisely、preciseness、imprecision。英语经法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one cut: a finely stated value, statistical repeatability, an instrument's smallest step, exact wording, targeted action, reliable digits, machining tolerance and strict legal form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守着同一刀：精细报出的测量值、统计上的重复一致性、仪器的最小刻度、确切的措辞、定点干预、可靠位数、加工公差，以及法律形式上的严格精确。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin blade cutting away everything that is not the exact point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把薄刃削掉一切不属于那一点的部分。

branches.en: FINE DIVISIONS: stating a value in narrow steps and counting the reliable digits are the same cut seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 细分：把值报成窄小的台阶与数出可靠位数，是同一刀的两面。

branches.en: REPEATS AGREE: statistical precision is the spread among repeats, not the distance from the truth.
branches.cn: 重复一致：统计上的精密度是重复测量之间的散布，而不是与真值的距离。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT'S EDGE: a finer scale lets a device separate what a coarse one merges.
branches.cn: 仪器的刃口：刻度更细的装置能把粗装置混在一起的值分开。

branches.en: CLEAN WORDING: exact speech and strict legal form both cut off every second reading.
branches.cn: 干净的措辞：确切的表达与严格的法律形式，都切掉了第二种读法。

branches.en: ACTION AT ONE SPOT: precision farming and precision machining both demand the cut land where the work requires.
branches.cn: 定点下手：精准农业与精密加工都要求这一刀落在工作真正需要的地方。

intro.en: Precision is a Latin noun of action built from a prefix, a verb root and a suffix, and the same pieces also build the everyday adjectives precise and imprecise.
intro.cn: precision 是由前缀、动词词根与后缀构成的拉丁动作名词，同样的构件也造出日常形容词 precise 与 imprecise。

latinIntro.en: Prae- 'in front' plus caedere 'to cut' yields praecidere, and -io turns it into the action noun praecisio; English then adds -ly and -ness and negates the whole word with im-.
latinIntro.cn: prae-「在前」加 caedere「切」得到 praecidere，-io 把它变成动作名词 praecisio；英语再加上 -ly 与 -ness，并用 im- 否定整个词。

items.example: The prefix puts the cutting ahead of the thing cut.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把切割放在被切之物的前面。

items.example: Incision and excise share this verb.
items.exampleCN: incision 与 excise 共用这个动词。

items.example: A long speech could be cut down to a short one.
items.exampleCN: 一段长话可以被截短成几句。

items.example: The Latin noun already carried the idea of trimming to the right size.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词已经含有「削到恰好」的意思。

items.example: The word moved from speech to instruments.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从言辞转到了仪器上。

items.example: A precise answer leaves no room for a second reading.
items.exampleCN: 确切的回答不给第二种读法留空间。
这些零件严丝合缝地拼在一起。

items.example: Any imprecision in the clock ruins the timing.
items.exampleCN: 时钟的任何不精确都会毁掉计时。

items.example: An imprecise word can start a quarrel.
items.exampleCN: 一个不准确的词就能引起争吵。

items.example: Her preciseness made the instructions easy to follow.
items.exampleCN: 她的一丝不苟让说明容易照着做。

definition_zh: 捕食者；掠食者；掠夺者
definition_en: an organism that hunts and kills others for food, or a person, firm or state that exploits weaker parties
core_image: 一头狮子伏在草坡后，目光锁定饮水处的羚羊群
scene: 这里指「捕食者」。 The lion is the only apex predator left in this valley.
sceneCN: 这里 predator 指「捕食者」（第 1 个义项：捕杀其他动物为食的生物）；狮子是这片谷地仅存的顶级捕食者。图中可辨识物件：狮子、草坡、羚羊群、水坑。

pos.zh: 捕食者；掠食者；掠夺者（可数，指动物或个人、机构）

collocations.zh: 顶级捕食者；食物链顶端物种
捕食者控制；为保护其他物种而猎杀捕食者
捕食者饱和；靠同步大量繁殖降低被捕食比例
企业掠食者；敌意收购者

derivatives.zh: 捕食性的；掠食的（异体 predaceous）

senses.title: An animal that hunts
senses.titleCN: 捕食动物：以捕杀为生的生物
senses.definition: an animal that captures and kills other animals for food
senses.definitionCN: 指通过捕获并杀死其他动物来获得食物的动物
senses.example: Wolves are social predators that hunt in coordinated packs.
senses.exampleCN: 狼是群居捕食者，以协同的群体方式狩猎。
senses.why: The core sense names a role in the food web, defined by behaviour rather than by species or diet alone.
senses.whyCN: 核心义项命名食物网中的一种角色，由行为而非仅仅由物种或食性界定。

senses.title: Apex predator
senses.titleCN: 顶级捕食者：成年个体几乎没有天敌
senses.definition: a predator at the top of its food chain, with no regular natural predator of its own
senses.definitionCN: 指处于食物链顶端、自身没有常规天敌的捕食者
senses.example: Removing the apex predator allowed deer to overgraze the forest floor.
senses.exampleCN: 移除顶级捕食者后，鹿群把林下植被啃食过度。
senses.why: The term marks a position rather than a behaviour: the top predator regulates everything below it.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法标出的是位置而非行为：顶级捕食者调节其下所有层级。

senses.title: A person who exploits
senses.titleCN: 掠夺者：以弱者为目标的个人
senses.definition: a person who systematically exploits vulnerable people for money, power or sexual gratification
senses.definitionCN: 指为金钱、权力或性满足而系统性剥削弱势者的个人
senses.example: The court described the recruiter as a predator who targeted teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭把那名招募者描述为专门针对青少年的掠夺者。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the hunt: the vulnerable are stalked, isolated and consumed, and the harm is one-sided.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了捕猎：弱势者被跟踪、被孤立、被吞食，伤害是单向的。

senses.title: Corporate predator
senses.titleCN: 企业掠食者：以收购吞并对手的公司
senses.definition: a company that grows by aggressively buying or dismantling weaker firms
senses.definitionCN: 指通过激进收购或拆解较弱企业而壮大的公司
senses.example: The family-owned mill was bought by a corporate predator and closed within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家家族磨坊被一家企业掠食者买下，一年内即关闭。
senses.why: Finance borrowed the animal word for the firm that treats other firms as prey rather than partners.
senses.whyCN: 金融借用了动物词汇，指把其他公司当猎物而非伙伴的企业。

senses.title: Microbial predator
senses.titleCN: 微生物捕食者：猎杀细菌的单细胞生物
senses.definition: a bacterium or protist that kills and consumes other microbes
senses.definitionCN: 指杀死并消耗其他微生物的细菌或原生生物
senses.example: The soil bacterium is a microbial predator that drills into other cells.
senses.exampleCN: 这种土壤细菌是微生物捕食者，能钻入其他细胞。
senses.why: Scale shrinks but the role survives: a predator still captures and consumes, even without a mouth.
senses.whyCN: 尺度缩小了，角色却保留：即使没有嘴，捕食者仍然捕获并消耗。

senses.title: Half of a predator-prey pair
senses.titleCN: 捕食对的一半：与猎物相互定义
senses.definition: the hunting side of a paired relationship whose two populations rise and fall together
senses.definitionCN: 指成对关系中的狩猎一方，两个种群数量随之共同涨落
senses.example: The predator and its prey oscillate on offset cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 捕食者与猎物在错开的周期上振荡。
senses.why: Neither side can be defined alone: a predator is whatever eats the prey, and the prey is whatever the predator eats.
senses.whyCN: 任何一方都无法单独定义：捕食者就是吃猎物的一方，猎物就是被捕食者吃的一方。

senses.title: Predator control
senses.titleCN: 捕食者控制：为保护目标物种而猎杀
senses.definition: in wildlife management, the deliberate reduction of predator numbers to protect livestock or endangered prey
senses.definitionCN: 野生动物管理中指为保护牲畜或濒危猎物而有意减少捕食者数量
senses.example: Predator control around the nesting grounds is debated every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 每年春天，巢区周围的捕食者控制都会引发争论。
senses.why: Management turns the predator into a variable to be adjusted, which is why the word appears in policy rather than only in biology.
senses.whyCN: 管理把捕食者变成可调节的变量，因此这个词不仅出现在生物学，也出现在政策里。

senses.title: Predator satiation
senses.titleCN: 捕食者饱和：以数量洪流换存活率
senses.definition: an evolutionary strategy in which prey reproduce in overwhelming numbers so that predators cannot eat them all
senses.definitionCN: 指猎物以压倒性数量同步繁殖、使捕食者吃不完的演化策略
senses.example: Bamboo masting relies on predator satiation to let some seeds survive.
senses.exampleCN: 竹子的集体结实依靠捕食者饱和，让部分种子得以存活。
senses.why: The term names the predator as a limiting filter: the strategy works only if the predator's appetite is finite.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法把捕食者当作限制性过滤器：策略生效的前提是捕食者的胃口有限。

intro.en: Predator is an English agent noun on Latin praedator 'plunderer', from praeda 'booty'. It began as a word for a raider before ecology made it a word for a hunter.
intro.cn: predator 是英语在拉丁语 praedator「劫掠者」上构成的施动名词，praedator 又出自 praeda「战利品」。它最初指劫掠者，后来被生态学变成捕猎者。

items.en: Praeda meant booty or prey, and the same root produced prey in French and predation in English.
items.cn: praeda 意为战利品或猎物，同一词根在法语中产生 prey，在英语中产生 predation。

items.en: Praedator named a plunderer or raider. Its suffix -tor marks the person who performs the act.
items.cn: praedator 指劫掠者、抢夺者，后缀 -tor 标出执行该行为的人。

items.en: English predator appears in the nineteenth century, first in the raiding sense. The exact first citation is uncertain, and it is generally placed around the 1860s to 1870s.
items.cn: 英语 predator 在 19 世纪出现，最初取劫掠义；确切首见书证存疑，一般认为在 1860 至 1870 年代。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology made predator the standard word for a hunting animal, and the older human sense became figurative.
items.cn: 20 世纪生态学把 predator 定为狩猎动物的标准词，较早的人事义则退为比喻用法。

items.en: The word now covers corporate and criminal senses: a predator is anyone who treats others as expendable prey.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖企业与犯罪语境：凡把他人当作可消耗猎物的人，都可被称作 predator。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the actor, the act and the prey; the near-meaning group separates a behavioural role from a dietary class.
note.cn: 形近组区分施动者、行为与猎物；近义组区分行为角色与食性类别。

entries.definition: The process or event of killing and eating. A predator performs predation; predation is not the animal itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指杀死并取食的过程或事件。捕食者实施捕食；捕食不是动物本身。

entries.definition: Describes the hunting or exploitative quality. It modifies behaviour, prices or firms, not the animal as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 描述捕猎或掠夺的性质，修饰行为、价格或企业，而不是作为名词指动物。

entries.tag: an older synonym for the adjective
entries.definition: A variant adjective meaning hunting or predatory, usually of insects and other invertebrates. It is not the noun for the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词异体，意为捕食的，多用于昆虫及其他无脊椎动物。它不是指动物的名词。

entries.definition: An animal whose diet is mainly flesh. A carnivore need not hunt, since it may be a scavenger, and a predator need not be a mammal.
entries.definitionCN: 指以肉食为主的动物。食肉动物未必捕猎，因为它可能是食腐者；捕食者也未必是哺乳动物。

entries.definition: One that pursues game. It stresses the chase and is used of humans as well as animals, while predator stresses the ecological role.
entries.definitionCN: 指追逐猎物者，强调追捕过程，可用于人也可用于动物；predator 则强调生态角色。

entries.definition: An organism that feeds on a host without usually killing it. It exploits, but it does not hunt and consume in the predatory sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指寄生于宿主、通常不杀死宿主的生物。它也剥削，但不进行捕食意义上的猎杀与吞食。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: praeda 'booty' plus -tor 'one who': the one who takes.
normal.cn: praeda「战利品」加 -tor「做某事的人」：取走东西的那一方。

normal.en: The family runs predation, predatory, predacious, prey and depredation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 predation、predatory、predacious、prey、depredation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: apex predator, natural predator, predator control, predator satiation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：顶级捕食者、天敌、捕食者控制、捕食者饱和。

normal.en: A predator hunts; a carnivore eats meat. A scavenger may be a carnivore but not a predator.
normal.cn: 捕食者狩猎；食肉动物吃肉。食腐者可以是食肉动物，却不是捕食者。

normal.en: In business the word becomes corporate predator: a buyer that treats firms as prey.
normal.cn: 在商业中这个词变成企业掠食者：把公司当猎物的买家。

abstract.en: Picture a lion low in the grass, eyes fixed on the herd at the water.
abstract.cn: 想象狮子压低身子伏在草里，眼睛盯住水边的兽群。

abstract.en: Picture a bacterium drilling into another cell and draining it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个细菌钻进另一个细胞并把它吸干。

abstract.en: Picture a fund buying a struggling factory, selling its machines and closing its gates.
abstract.cn: 想象一家基金买下经营困难的工厂，卖掉机器，关上大门。

examples.en: The removal of the apex predator changed the whole riverbank.
examples.cn: 顶级捕食者的消失改变了整片河岸。

examples.en: The bacterium is a predator of other microbes in the soil.
examples.cn: 这种细菌是土壤中其他微生物的捕食者。

examples.en: Regulators accused the fund of acting as a corporate predator.
examples.cn: 监管者指责该基金扮演企业掠食者的角色。

dict_mnemonic.text: preda（猎物）+ tor（者）→ 取走猎物的一方 → predator 捕食者

root: 拉丁 praeda「战利品、猎物」→ praedator「劫掠者」→ 英语 predator；20 世纪起成为生态学中「捕食者」的标准词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one role: the stronger party that takes. The prey may be a mouse, a microbe, a rival firm or a vulnerable person.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一角色：取走东西的强势一方。猎物可以是老鼠、微生物、对手企业或弱势个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lion in the grass watching the herd at the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：草丛中的狮子盯着水边的兽群。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL ROLE: capture and consumption define the predator at every scale.
branches.cn: 动物角色：捕获与消耗在一切尺度上界定捕食者。

branches.en: POSITION: the apex predator is defined by having no predator above it.
branches.cn: 位置：顶级捕食者由「上方没有捕食者」来界定。

branches.en: PAIRING AND MANAGEMENT: the predator is half of a cycle, a target of culling and a limit that prey can satiate.
branches.cn: 配对与管理：捕食者既是周期的一半，也是被猎杀的对象，还是猎物可以将其填饱的限制。

branches.en: CORPORATE METAPHOR: firms that treat others as prey inherit the old raider sense.
branches.cn: 企业隐喻：把他人当作猎物的公司，继承了古老的掠夺者含义。

branches.en: THE WORD ITSELF: Latin praedator was a plunderer before it was a hunter.
branches.cn: 词本身：拉丁语 praedator 先指劫掠者，后指猎手。

intro.en: Predator is a Latin agent noun, so its ending -tor tells you it names the one who performs the act.
intro.cn: predator 是拉丁施动名词，结尾 -tor 告诉你它指执行该行为的一方。

latinIntro.en: Praeda is the root, praedari the verb, and -tor the agent suffix that English keeps in predator and competitor.
latinIntro.cn: praeda 是词根，praedari 是动词，-tor 是施动后缀，英语在 predator 与 competitor 中保留了它。

items.example: The hawk is a daytime predator.
items.exampleCN: 鹰是白昼活动的捕食者。

items.meaning: the act of hunting and eating
items.exampleCN: 捕食限制了啮齿动物数量。
这家公司采用了掠夺性定价。
捕食性甲虫能控制蚜虫。

items.structure: Old French preie, from Latin praeda
items.example: The prey froze when the shadow passed.
items.exampleCN: 影子掠过时，猎物僵住了。

items.example: The flock's depredation ruined the crop.
items.exampleCN: 鸟群的掠夺毁掉了庄稼。

items.example: The island was predator-free before the rats arrived.
items.exampleCN: 老鼠到来前，这座岛没有捕食者。
该模型追踪捕食者与猎物周期。

items.example: The report noted the fund's predatoriness.
items.exampleCN: 报告指出了该基金的掠夺性。

definition_zh: 捕食性的；掠夺性的；剥削性的
definition_en: describing an animal or behaviour that hunts and kills, or an act that exploits a weaker party for gain

scene: 这里指「捕食性的」。 Predatory birds circle above the marsh, forcing the rodents to stay under cover.
sceneCN: 这里 predatory 指「捕食性的」（第 1 个义项：以猎杀其他动物为生）；捕食性鸟类在沼泽上空盘旋，迫使啮齿动物躲在掩护下。图中可辨识物件：鹰、上升气流、田鼠洞、沼泽。
