senses.title: Hunting for food
senses.titleCN: 捕食性：以猎杀其他动物为生
senses.definition: describing an animal or species that hunts and kills other animals for food
senses.definitionCN: 描述以猎杀其他动物获取食物的动物或物种
senses.example: Predatory fish control the smaller species in the reef lagoon.
senses.exampleCN: 捕食性鱼类控制着礁湖中的小型物种。
senses.why: This is the literal base: the adjective marks a hunting way of life rather than a particular species.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面本义：这个形容词标出的是一种狩猎式的生活方式，而不是某个特定物种。

senses.title: Predatory pricing
senses.titleCN: 掠夺性定价：低价挤垮对手再抬价
senses.definition: in competition law, pricing below cost in order to eliminate rivals and then raise prices
senses.definitionCN: 竞争法中指以低于成本的价格消灭对手、随后再抬价的作法
senses.example: The airline was fined for predatory pricing on one regional route.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司因在一条区域航线上掠夺性定价而被罚款。
senses.why: The adjective marks intent: the low price is not generosity but a trap for competitors.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出意图：低价不是慷慨，而是给竞争者设的陷阱。

senses.title: Predatory lending
senses.titleCN: 掠夺性放贷：以不公平条件套住借款人
senses.definition: describing loans with unfair terms, hidden fees or interest designed to trap vulnerable borrowers
senses.definitionCN: 描述条款不公、费用隐蔽或利息设计成套住弱势借款人的贷款
senses.example: The regulator banned several predatory lending practices in the payday market.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者禁止了发薪日贷款市场中的若干掠夺性放贷做法。
senses.why: The prey here is a borrower, and the trap replaces the teeth: the harm comes from contract terms, not force.
senses.whyCN: 这里的猎物是借款人，合同条款代替了牙齿：伤害来自条文，而非暴力。

senses.title: Exploitative behaviour
senses.titleCN: 掠夺性行为：对弱势者的系统性剥削
senses.definition: describing conduct that targets vulnerable people and treats them as objects to be used
senses.definitionCN: 描述以弱势者为目标、把他们当作可使用之物的行为
senses.example: The inquiry found a pattern of predatory behavior toward young recruits.
senses.exampleCN: 调查发现了一种针对年轻新人的掠夺性行为模式。
senses.why: The adjective carries moral weight in this sense: it says the stronger party selected weakness on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在此义带有道德重量：它表明强势方是有意挑选弱者的。

senses.title: Predatory journal
senses.titleCN: 掠夺性期刊：收费而不审稿的出版陷阱
senses.definition: describing a publisher that charges authors fees while providing no real peer review or editorial service
senses.definitionCN: 描述只向作者收费、却不提供真正同行评审或编辑服务的出版方
senses.example: The librarian warned students away from predatory journals.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆员提醒学生远离掠夺性期刊。
senses.why: Academic publishing borrowed the word because the target is a researcher's need for publication, not their wallet alone.
senses.whyCN: 学术出版借用这个词，因为目标不只是钱包，还有研究者对发表的迫切需求。

senses.title: Predatory acquisition
senses.titleCN: 掠夺性收购：买下并拆解目标公司
senses.definition: describing a takeover whose aim is to strip assets or eliminate a competitor rather than to run the business
senses.definitionCN: 描述以剥离资产或消灭竞争者而非经营企业为目的的收购
senses.example: Workers called the takeover predatory because the buyer had already closed two rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 工人称这次收购是掠夺性的，因为买家此前已关掉两家对手。
senses.why: The financial sense keeps the hunting frame: the acquired firm is consumed, not merged with.
senses.whyCN: 金融义保留了捕猎框架：被收购的公司是被吞食，而不是被合并。

senses.title: Predatory instincts
senses.titleCN: 捕食本能：行为层面的猎杀冲动
senses.definition: describing innate behavioural drives in an animal that lead it to stalk, chase and kill
senses.definitionCN: 描述动物身上导致其跟踪、追逐与杀死的先天行为驱力
senses.example: The kitten's predatory instinct appeared before it could hunt successfully.
senses.exampleCN: 幼猫的捕食本能在它真正会狩猎之前就已显现。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes an internal drive rather than an ecological role, moving from the food web to behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个形容词描述内在驱力而非生态角色，从食物网移到行为学。

senses.title: Predatory in nature writing
senses.titleCN: 自然写作中的掠食意象：美学化的猛禽
senses.definition: used in nature writing and poetry to describe the beauty and threat of a hunter, often with admiration
senses.definitionCN: 在自然写作与诗歌中描述猎手的美感与威胁，常带赞赏
senses.example: The poem fixes on the predatory stillness of the hawk before it drops.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗聚焦于鹰俯冲前那种捕食者的静止。
senses.why: The same adjective can be admiring rather than condemnatory when the context is wild nature instead of markets.
senses.whyCN: 当语境是荒野而非市场时，同一个形容词可以是赞赏而非谴责。

intro.en: Predatory comes from Latin praedatorius 'of plunder', an adjective on praedator. English first used it of raiding and later of hunting.
intro.cn: predatory 出自拉丁语 praedatorius「劫掠的」，是 praedator 的形容词。英语先用它指劫掠，后用于捕猎。

items.en: The adjective praedatorius described what belongs to plunder or a plunderer. Its stem is praeda 'booty'.
items.cn: 形容词 praedatorius 描述属于劫掠或劫掠者的事物，其词干是 praeda「战利品」。

items.en: Predatory entered English in the seventeenth century in the sense of plundering. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: predatory 在 17 世纪进入英语，取劫掠义；确切首见书证存疑。

items.en: As natural history grew in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, the adjective shifted toward animals that live by hunting.
items.cn: 随着 18、19 世纪博物学发展，这个形容词转向指以狩猎为生的动物。

items.en: Twentieth-century law produced predatory pricing and predatory lending, where the adjective marks deliberate harm to weaker parties.
items.cn: 20 世纪法律造出掠夺性定价与掠夺性放贷，此时形容词标出对弱势方的有意伤害。

items.en: The phrase predatory journal spread in the twenty-first century with open-access publishing, and its boundaries are still debated.
items.cn: 掠夺性期刊这一说法随开放获取出版在 21 世纪扩散，其边界至今仍有争论。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the adjective from its noun relatives; the near-meaning group separates predatory from merely aggressive or parasitic.
note.cn: 形近组把这个形容词与名词同族词分开；近义组区分掠夺性与单纯强势或寄生。

entries.definition: The animal or party that hunts. It is a count noun, so it cannot stand where an adjective is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 指狩猎的动物或一方。它是可数名词，不能放在需要形容词的位置。

entries.definition: The process of killing and eating. Predatory describes the quality; predation names the process.
entries.definitionCN: 指杀死并取食的过程。predatory 描述性质，predation 命名过程。

entries.definition: A rarer adjective with the same hunting sense, now mostly used of insects. It is not interchangeable with the noun predator.
entries.definitionCN: 较罕见的同义形容词，如今多用于昆虫。它不能与名词 predator 互换。

entries.definition: Means grasping and greedy, usually of people or institutions. It condemns appetite for gain and is never used for a hawk.
entries.definitionCN: 意为贪婪攫取的，通常用于人或机构。它谴责对利益的贪欲，从不用于鹰。

entries.definition: Describes unfair use of others. It is the plain-language equivalent of figurative predatory, without the animal image.
entries.definitionCN: 描述不公平地利用他人。它是比喻义 predatory 的平实说法，不含动物意象。

entries.definition: Describes feeding on a host that usually survives. Predatory behaviour kills or destroys, while parasitic behaviour drains.
entries.definitionCN: 描述以通常仍存活的宿主为食。掠夺性行为会杀死或摧毁，寄生性行为则慢慢吸取。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: predator + -y: having the nature of a predator.
normal.cn: predator + -y：具有捕食者性质的。

normal.en: Typical phrases: predatory pricing, predatory lending, predatory behavior, predatory journal.
normal.cn: 典型搭配：掠夺性定价、掠夺性放贷、掠夺性行为、掠夺性期刊。

normal.en: The family runs predator, predation, predacious, predatorily and predatoriness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 predator、predation、predacious、predatorily、predatoriness。

normal.en: Rapacious is greedy; predatory is hunting. Only the first names an appetite.
normal.cn: rapacious 指贪婪；predatory 指捕猎。只有前者命名一种欲望。

normal.en: The same adjective can condemn a lender or admire a hawk, depending on context.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词可以谴责放贷者，也可以赞赏鹰，取决于语境。

abstract.en: Picture a hawk circling without moving its wings, a shadow sliding over the marsh.
abstract.cn: 想象鹰不扇翅地盘旋，影子滑过沼泽。

abstract.en: Picture a payday office on a poor street, its sign promising cash and its contract hiding fees.
abstract.cn: 想象贫困街区的一家发薪日贷款门店，招牌承诺现金，合同却藏着费用。

abstract.en: Picture a journal that accepts a paper in two days and sends an invoice the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一本期刊两天内接收论文，第二天就寄来账单。

examples.en: Predatory birds keep the marsh rodents under dense cover.
examples.cn: 捕食性鸟类让沼泽里的啮齿动物躲在密丛下。

examples.en: The court found the below-cost pricing predatory.
examples.cn: 法院认定这种低于成本的定价属掠夺性定价。

examples.en: Students were warned about predatory journals that mimic legitimate titles.
examples.cn: 学生们被提醒警惕那些模仿正规刊名的掠夺性期刊。

dict_mnemonic.text: predator（捕食者）+ y（……的）→ 像捕食者一样的 → predatory 掠夺性的

root: 拉丁 praeda「战利品」→ praedator「劫掠者」→ praedatorius「劫掠的」→ 英语 predatory；后由「劫掠」转为「捕食」与「掠夺性」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all modify something with a hunting quality: a bird, a price, a loan, a journal or an instinct.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都用这个形容词修饰某种带有捕猎性质的东西：鸟、价格、贷款、期刊或本能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hawk circling over the marsh while a shadow slides across the grass.
core.cn: 核心意象：鹰在沼泽上空盘旋，影子滑过草地。

branches.en: THE INSTINCT: a hunting drive written into behaviour.
branches.cn: 捕食本能：写进行为层面的猎杀驱力。

branches.en: MARKETS: price and credit become traps set for rivals and borrowers.
branches.cn: 市场：价格与信贷变成给对手和借款人设下的陷阱。

branches.en: CONDUCT: the adjective condemns deliberate targeting of vulnerability.
branches.cn: 行为：这个形容词谴责有意挑选弱点下手。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: journals and acquirers consume the party they pretend to serve.
branches.cn: 机构：期刊与收购方吞食它们声称服务的对象。

branches.en: DOUBLE TONE: literal hunting and poetry's admiring eye share one adjective.
branches.cn: 双重语气：字面的猎食与诗歌里欣赏的目光共用同一个形容词。

intro.en: Predatory is a Latin adjective ending in -ory, built on the agent noun for a plunderer.
intro.cn: predatory 是以 -ory 结尾的拉丁形容词，建立在表示劫掠者的施动名词之上。

latinIntro.en: Praeda is the root, -ator the agent, and -orius the adjective suffix meaning 'belonging to'.
latinIntro.cn: praeda 是词根，-ator 是施动成分，-orius 是意为「属于……」的形容词后缀。

items.meaning: of or like a plunderer or hunter
items.meaningCN: 属于劫掠者或猎手的，或像其一样的
items.example: The firm's predatory tactics drew scrutiny.
items.exampleCN: 该公司的掠夺性策略引来审查。

items.example: The predator waited at the water hole.
Predation fell after the pack moved north.

items.structure: Old French preie, from Latin praeda
items.example: The prey ran for the treeline.
Depredation by gulls emptied the nests.
items.exampleCN: 海鸥的劫掠清空了鸟巢。

items.example: The lender acted predatorily toward desperate borrowers.
items.exampleCN: 放贷者对走投无路的借款人采取掠夺性做法。

items.example: Critics noted the predatoriness of the business model.
items.exampleCN: 批评者指出了该商业模式的掠夺性。

items.example: Rapacious landlords raised rents twice a year.
items.exampleCN: 贪婪的房东一年涨两次租。

definition_zh: 预测；预言；预报；预料；预示
definition_en: to say or state in advance that something will happen, especially on the basis of evidence or reasoning
core_image: 站在今天，用话把明天的那件事先说出来
scene: 经济学家预测明年的增长会放缓。Economists predict slower growth next year.
sceneCN: 这里 predict 是「依据数据对将来作出判断」（第 2 个义项：预测）；句意：经济学家预测明年增长会放缓。场景要点：用现有信息、指向未来、可被检验；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 预测；预言；预报；预料
作出预测；预言

derivatives.zh: 不可预测的；变化莫测的

senses.title: To say what will happen
senses.titleCN: 预测：先说将来会发生什么
senses.definition: to state in advance that a particular event will happen
senses.definitionCN: 事先说明某个特定事件将会发生
senses.example: No one could predict which team would win.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人能预测哪支队伍会赢。
senses.why: Latin praedicere is prae 'before' plus dicere 'say'. The plain sense is saying something before it becomes true.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praedicere 是 prae“在前”加 dicere“说”。最朴素的意思，就是在事情成真之前先把它说出来。

senses.title: To forecast from evidence
senses.titleCN: 预测：拿现有信息推算未来
senses.definition: to estimate a future state on the basis of data, models, or reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 依据数据、模型或推理估计未来的状况
senses.example: Economists predict slower growth next year.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家预测明年增长会放缓。
senses.why: The saying is not a guess but a calculation. Evidence is fed in, and the statement about the future comes out.
senses.whyCN: 这话不是猜的，而是算的。把证据喂进去，关于未来的陈述就出来了。

senses.title: Scientific prediction
senses.titleCN: 科学预言：理论先说出可检验的结果
senses.definition: to derive a testable consequence from a scientific theory before it is observed
senses.definitionCN: 在观察之前，从科学理论推出一个可检验的结果
senses.example: The theory predicted a new particle, which was found years later.
senses.exampleCN: 该理论预言了一种新粒子，数年后被找到。
senses.why: A good theory must be able to say what will be seen. Prediction is the test that separates science from speculation.
senses.whyCN: 好的理论必须能说出将会看到什么。预测是把科学与空想分开的那场考试。

senses.title: To indicate in advance by signs
senses.titleCN: 预示：迹象先替将来开口
senses.definition: to be a sign that something will happen, without anyone saying it in words
senses.definitionCN: 成为某事将会发生的迹象，而非由人用话说出
senses.example: Dark clouds predicted a heavy storm.
senses.exampleCN: 乌云预示着大风暴。
senses.why: Signs can speak. When the world itself shows what is coming, we extend the verb from the speaker to the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 迹象也能说话。当世界本身显露出即将发生的事，我们就把这个动词从说话者扩展到证据上。

senses.title: To prophesy
senses.titleCN: 预言：以先知的口吻宣告
senses.definition: to foretell future events as a prophet or oracle does, often without evidence
senses.definitionCN: 像先知或神谕那样预告未来，常无证据支持
senses.example: The old woman predicted that the drought would last seven years.
senses.exampleCN: 老妇人预言旱情会持续七年。
senses.why: The same act of speaking first, but the authority comes from revelation rather than from data.
senses.whyCN: 同样是先说出口的动作，只是权威来自启示而非数据。

senses.title: To expect or anticipate
senses.titleCN: 预料：心里已经先把它算上
senses.definition: to expect something to happen, often in everyday planning
senses.definitionCN: 预期某事会发生，常用于日常安排
senses.example: We predicted heavy traffic and left an hour early.
senses.exampleCN: 我们预料会堵车，所以提前一小时出发。
senses.why: Prediction need not be public. Private anticipation is the same forward-looking move, kept inside the head.
senses.whyCN: 预测不必公开。私下的预料是同一个朝前的动作，只是留在脑子里。

senses.title: Statistics: to estimate a value
senses.definition: to produce an estimated value for a future or unknown observation from a model
senses.definitionCN: 用模型为未来或未知的观测给出一个估计值
senses.example: The model predicts sales of 12,000 units in the first quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 模型预测第一季度销量为一万二千件。
senses.why: In statistics the prediction is a number with an interval, not a sentence. The verb becomes a technical operation.
senses.whyCN: 在统计学里，预测是一个带区间的数，而不是一句话。这个动词变成了一项技术操作。

senses.title: To warn in advance
senses.titleCN: 预告：提前提醒，好让人准备
senses.definition: to announce something in advance so that people can prepare for it
senses.definitionCN: 事先告知某事，以便人们可以准备
senses.example: The report predicted shortages and urged hospitals to stock up.
senses.exampleCN: 报告预告了短缺，并敦促医院囤货。
senses.why: Saying it early has a use: it buys time. Prediction becomes a warning when the future it names is unwelcome.
senses.whyCN: 提前说出来是有用的：它买来时间。当所命名的未来不受欢迎时，预测就成了预警。

intro.en: Predict is a Latin compound meaning to say beforehand. It is one of a large family built on the verb dicere, to say.
intro.cn: predict 是一个意为“事先说出”的拉丁复合词。它属于一个建立在动词 dicere（说）之上的大词族。

items.en: Dicere meant 'to say, declare'. It is the source of diction, dictionary, verdict, contradict, and predict.
items.cn: dicere 意为“说、宣告”。它是 diction、dictionary、verdict、contradict、predict 的来源。

items.en: Prae meant 'before, in front'. Joined to a verb of saying, it produces the sense of saying something before its time.
items.cn: prae 意为“在前”。与表示“说”的动词结合，就产生“在时间之前说出来”的意思。

items.en: Praedicere meant 'to make known beforehand, to declare in advance'. It was used for foretelling as well as for public proclamation.
items.cn: praedicere 意为“事先让人知道、预先宣告”。它既用于预言，也用于公开宣布。

items.en: The past participle praedictus meant 'foretold'. English keeps it inside words like prediction and predictably.
items.cn: 过去分词 praedictus 意为“被预言的”。英语把它保留在 prediction、predictably 这类词里。

items.en: English predict appears in the 16th century, at first in religious and learned writing about foretelling. The modern data-based sense develops much later.
items.cn: 英语 predict 出现于 16 世纪，最早见于谈论预言的宗教与学术写作。以数据为基础的现代义要晚得多才发展出来。

items.en: With the rise of science and statistics, predict becomes the standard word for evidence-based foretelling, while prophesy remains the religious term.
items.cn: 随着科学与统计的兴起，predict 成了“有据预告”的标准词，而 prophesy 保持宗教色彩。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for saying. The second group collects words for foretelling, each with a different basis of authority.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“说”的动词。第二组收表示“预告”的词，各自依据的权威不同。

entries.definition: a statement about what will happen. It is the noun built on predict with -ion.
entries.definitionCN: 关于将会发生什么的陈述。它是 predict 加 -ion 构成的名词。

entries.definition: able to be foreseen, often with a hint of dullness. Predict plus -able.
entries.definitionCN: 可以被预见的，常带一点乏味的暗示。predict 加 -able。

entries.definition: the part of a sentence that says something about the subject, or to base something on. It comes from Latin praedicare, a cousin of praedicere.
entries.definitionCN: 句子中陈述主语的部分，或“以……为依据”。它来自拉丁 praedicare，是 praedicere 的近亲。

entries.definition: a decision or judgement. Ver- 'true' plus dict 'said': what is said as true.
entries.definitionCN: 裁决或判定。ver-“真”加 dict“说”：被说成真实的话。

entries.definition: to say what is likely in weather, economics, or other systems. Forecast is common for weather and trends; predict is the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 预告天气、经济或其他系统的可能状况。forecast 多用于天气与趋势；predict 是一般用语。

entries.definition: to tell of a future event. Foretell is literary and often implies a sign or a seer.
entries.definitionCN: 讲述未来的事件。foretell 带文学色彩，常暗示有征兆或预言者。

entries.definition: to foretell under divine inspiration. Prophesy claims a religious authority that predict does not.
entries.definitionCN: 在神圣启示下预告未来。prophesy 主张一种宗教权威，predict 没有这种主张。

entries.definition: to expect something and often act in advance. Anticipate adds preparation; predict can be purely a statement.
entries.definitionCN: 预期某事并常提前行动。anticipate 多出“准备”之意；predict 可以只是陈述。

entries.definition: to estimate future figures from present trends. Project is technical and numerical, closer to sense 07.
entries.definitionCN: 由当前趋势估算未来数字。project 是技术性、数值性的，更接近第 7 义项。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the sentence said too early, the economist's model, the particle found later, the dark clouds, and the shopping list made before the rush.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：提早说出的那句话、经济学家的模型、后来找到的粒子、乌云、以及抢购前先列好的清单。

normal.en: Pre- means before, dict means say. Predict is say-before.
normal.cn: pre- 是“在前”，dict 是“说”。predict 就是“先说”。

normal.en: A weather forecast and a stock forecast are both predict with numbers plugged in.
normal.cn: 天气预报和股市预测，都是把数字代进去的 predict。

normal.en: A theory predicts a particle, then the lab goes looking for it. Prediction is the theory's exam.
normal.cn: 理论预言一种粒子，实验室随后去找它。预测就是理论的那场考试。

normal.en: Dark clouds predict rain without saying a word: signs can also speak.
normal.cn: 乌云一言不发就预示下雨：迹象也会说话。

normal.en: Predicting a rush and leaving early is the same verb, just kept private.
normal.cn: 预料拥堵并提早出门，是同一个动词，只是留在心里。

abstract.en: Every prediction is a promise the present makes about the future, and it can be broken by a single unforeseen event.
abstract.cn: 每个预测都是现在对未来作出的承诺，而它可能被一个未预见的事件打破。

abstract.en: The difference between prophecy and prediction is not the content but the warrant: revelation versus evidence.
abstract.cn: 预言与预测的差别不在内容，而在凭据：是启示，还是证据。

abstract.en: To predict well is to be willing to be wrong in public, which is why science prizes it.
abstract.cn: 预测得好，意味着愿意在公众面前出错；正因如此，科学看重它。

examples.en: The model predicts that sea levels will rise by about half a metre this century.
examples.cn: 该模型预测本世纪海平面将上升约半米。

examples.en: As predicted, the first frost came in the last week of October.
examples.cn: 正如所料，初霜在十月最后一周到来。

examples.en: Analysts predict a sharp fall in demand for new cars.
examples.cn: 分析人士预测新车需求将大幅下降。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞迪克特”——普瑞提前把“迪克特”那件事说出口，就是 predict（预测）

root: 拉丁语 praedicere“事先说出、预先宣告”＝prae“在前”+ dicere“说” → 英语 predict（16 世纪）；与 diction、dictionary、verdict、contradict 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The word always means saying something before it happens. What changes is the basis: evidence, theory, signs, revelation, private expectation, or a statistical model. Each basis gives a slightly different shade of the same forward-speaking act.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词始终指“在事情发生之前先说出来”。变化的是依据：证据、理论、征兆、启示、私下预期，或统计模型。每一种依据都给同一个“朝前说话”的动作一种不同的色调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence spoken today about an event that has not yet arrived.
core.cn: 核心意象：今天说出一句话，说的是尚未到来的事件。

branches.en: SPEECH: saying or expecting, public or private.
branches.cn: 言语：说出或预料，公开或私下。

branches.en: CALCULATION: forecasts from data, and statistical estimates.
branches.cn: 计算：由数据作出的预报，以及统计估计。

branches.en: SCIENCE: the theory that names a result before it is observed.
branches.cn: 科学：在结果被观察之前就把它命名的理论。

branches.en: SIGN AND WARNING: the world speaking through evidence, and the early notice that buys time.
branches.cn: 征兆与预警：世界借证据说话，以及买来时间的提前告知。

branches.en: PROPHECY: the same act, warranted by revelation.
branches.cn: 预言：同一个动作，凭据是启示。

intro.en: Predict is one compound from the large dicere family. Every word below is either a piece of that compound or a sibling built with another prefix on the same verb of saying.
intro.cn: predict 是 dicere 大词族里的一个复合词。下面每个词，要么是这个复合词的构件，要么是在同一个“说”的动词上加别的前缀构成的兄弟词。

latinIntro.en: Latin praedicere and its participle praedictus supplied the English forms; the same dic- stem appears across law, grammar, and everyday speech.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 praedicere 及其分词 praedictus 提供了英语形式；同一个 dic- 词干出现在法律、语法与日常言语中。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀

definition_zh: 可预测的；可预料的；意料之中的；平淡老套的；规律稳定的
definition_en: able to be known or stated in advance; happening as everyone already expects; too regular to be interesting; and steady enough to be relied on
core_image: 老人的手在桌面上按同一节奏敲着，节拍一下都不差
scene: 老朋友聚会，话题总是从天气开始，再绕回谁又长胖了、谁换了工作。The conversation followed its predictable course: weather first, then who had gained weight.
sceneCN: 这里 predictable 指「可预料的、不出所料的」（第 2 个义项：事情按大家预想的样子发生）；句意为谈话照着可以预料的路子走：先说天气，再说谁胖了。图中可辨识场景：围坐的老朋友、从天气开头的话题、彼此打趣的笑声。

pos.zh: 可预测的；可预料的；平淡老套的；规律稳定的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 praedicere 经英语改造而来，义为「预言；预测」
由 predict 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「预言；预测」
由 predictable 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可预测性」
由否定前缀 un- 与 predictable 复合而成，义为「不可预测的」

senses.title: Able to be stated in advance
senses.titleCN: 可预测的；可以预先断定的
senses.definition: able to be known or worked out in advance because the evidence or the pattern allows it
senses.definitionCN: 因为证据或规律足够，所以能够提前知道或推算出来
senses.example: The tide is predictable to within a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水涨落的时间可以预测到几分钟之内。
senses.why: Latin praedicere meant to say something beforehand, and -able turns that act into a possibility: whatever can be said before it happens is predictable.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praedicere 意为「预先说出」，-able 把这个动作变成一种可能性：凡能在发生之前被说出来的，就是可预测的。

senses.title: Happening as everyone already expects
senses.titleCN: 意料之中的；不出所料的
senses.definition: happening in the way most people already expect, so that it causes no surprise when it does
senses.definitionCN: 按多数人早已预想的样子发生，真的发生时谁都不觉意外
senses.example: The ending of the film was predictable from the first scene.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的结局从第一场戏就能料到。
senses.why: If a thing can be said before it happens, then when it happens nobody is surprised; the sense slides from what can be foretold to what is simply unsurprising.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既然能在发生前被说出来，它真的发生时谁也不会吃惊；词义就从「可以预言」滑到「本来就没什么意外」。

senses.title: Too regular to be interesting
senses.definition: too regular or conventional to hold interest, showing no invention and no surprise
senses.definitionCN: 过于规律或循规蹈矩，因而提不起兴趣，既无新意也无意外
senses.example: Critics called the sequel predictable and safe.
senses.exampleCN: 评论界说这部续集平淡无趣、四平八稳。
senses.why: A pattern regular enough to be foretold soon becomes a pattern with nothing new inside it, and the same adjective turns into mild blame.
senses.whyCN: 一个规律到能被预言的格局，很快就变成内里没有新东西的格局，同一个形容词于是带上轻微的责备。

senses.title: Steady enough to be relied on
senses.definition: of a supply, income or person: behaving in a steady way that plans can be built on
senses.definitionCN: 指供给、收入或人行为稳定，可以照着它做计划
senses.example: Farmers here prefer a predictable supply of water to a lucky season.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的农户更想要稳定的供水，而不是碰运气的丰水季。
senses.why: When the certainty is useful rather than boring, the word becomes praise: a predictable supply is one that a plan can be built on.
senses.whyCN: 当这种确定性是有用的而不是无聊的，这个词就变成称赞：可预测的供给，就是能照着它做计划的供给。

intro.en: Predictable is predict plus -able. The Latin verb behind predict meant to say a thing beforehand, and English first used it for declaring rather than for foretelling.
intro.cn: predictable 是 predict 加 -able。predict 背后的拉丁动词意为「预先说出」，而英语最初用它表示宣称、断言，并非预言。

items.en: Dicere meant to say or to declare, and it stands behind a very large family of English words about speech.
items.cn: dicere 意为说、宣称，是英语里一大批与言语有关的词的源头。

items.en: Praedicare joined prae-, before, with dicere: to say beforehand, and also to proclaim something publicly.
items.cn: praedicare 把 prae-（在前）与 dicere 结合：预先说出，也指当众宣告。

items.en: The noun praedictio meant a foretelling or a prophecy, and it kept the solemn tone of announcing what is to come.
items.cn: 名词 praedictio 意为预言、预告，保留了宣告未来之事的庄重语气。

items.en: English predict first meant to declare or assert something, and only later settled on foretelling the future.
items.cn: 英语 predict 最早意为宣称、断言某事，后来才固定为「预言未来」。

items.en: The adjective was formed with -able in the nineteenth century, first for events, then for people and their dull habits.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十九世纪由 -able 构成，先用于事件，随后用于人及其乏味的习惯。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb of saying through the English family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what can be counted on.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「说」的拉丁动词，收它在英语里的一族词；近义组收表示「可以指望」的形容词。

entries.definition: To say what will happen before it does.
entries.definitionCN: 在事情发生之前说出它会发生。

entries.definition: A statement about what will happen in the future.
entries.definitionCN: 关于将来会发生什么的说法；预言。

entries.definition: Impossible to know in advance, often changing without warning.
entries.definitionCN: 无法提前知道的；常指变化无常。

entries.definition: The quality of being able to be known in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 可以提前知道的性质；可预测性。

entries.definition: Able to be known or expected in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 能够提前知道或料到的。

entries.definition: Thought likely to happen or to be the case.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为很可能发生或属实的。

entries.definition: Following a fixed pattern, with equal gaps between events.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定规律出现的；间隔均匀的。

entries.definition: Ordinary, repeated and part of the usual order of things.
entries.definitionCN: 平常而反复的，属于常规安排的。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from a Latin verb of saying beforehand, so its centre is speech: what can be said in advance, and then what has nothing left to say.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「预先说出」的拉丁动词上，中心是「说」：能提前说出来的，以及后来没什么可说的。

normal.en: Dicere is to say and prae- is before, so predict is literally to say before, and -able makes it possible to do so.
normal.cn: dicere 是说，prae- 是在前，所以 predict 字面就是「预先说」，-able 让它成为「可以预先说的」。

normal.en: Prediction is the noun in -ion, and it can be a weather forecast or a prophecy.
normal.cn: prediction 是加 -ion 的名词，可以是天气预报，也可以是预言。

normal.en: Unpredictable adds un-, and it is the word used for weather, toddlers and market prices.
normal.cn: unpredictable 加了否定前缀 un-，天气、幼儿和市场价格都常被这样形容。

normal.en: Predictability names the quality, and planners pay for it in supply chains.
normal.cn: predictability 指这种性质，供应链上的规划者愿意为它花钱。

normal.en: Predictable income is praise, predictable plot is blame: the same word, two directions of judgement.
normal.cn: predictable income 是称赞，predictable plot 是贬斥：同一个词，两个方向的评价。

abstract.en: To predict is to speak before the event; to be predictable is to leave the future no room to speak.
abstract.cn: predict 是在事情之前说话；predictable 则是不给未来留下说话的空间。

abstract.en: The word measures the distance between what we know and what happens, and that distance can be comfort or boredom.
abstract.cn: 这个词量的是「我们所知」与「实际发生」之间的距离，而这段距离可以是安心，也可以是无聊。

abstract.en: A predictable world is easy to live in and hard to be surprised by, and the adjective holds both halves.
abstract.cn: 可预测的世界住起来省心，却很难再有惊喜，这个形容词把两半都装着。

examples.en: The tide is predictable to within a few minutes.
examples.cn: 潮水涨落的时间可以预测到几分钟之内。

examples.en: The ending of the film was predictable from the first scene.
examples.cn: 这部电影的结局从第一场戏就能料到。

examples.en: Farmers here prefer a predictable supply of water.
examples.cn: 这里的农户更喜欢稳定的供水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞迪克特波」——提前把话说明白，事情照着走；predictable 就是可预测的。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ dicere（说）→ praedicere（预先说出）→ 名词 praedictio（预言）→ 英语 predict → 加 -able 成 predictable。同族有 prediction、unpredictable。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move along one line: what can be said in advance, what therefore surprises nobody, what becomes dull through repetition, and what is steady enough to build a plan on.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项沿着一条线移动：能提前说出的，因此谁都不意外的，因重复而变得乏味的，以及稳定到可以据之做计划的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old hand tapping the table in the same rhythm, beat after beat, without one missed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只苍老的手在桌面上按同一节奏敲着，一下接一下，一次不差。

branches.en: a tide table marked to the minute
branches.cn: 精确到分钟的潮汐表

branches.en: an audience guessing the ending before it comes
branches.cn: 观众在结局到来前就猜到了

branches.en: a sequel that repeats every turn of the first film
branches.cn: 把第一部每个转折都重来一遍的续集

branches.en: an irrigation channel running on schedule
branches.cn: 按日程放水的灌溉渠

branches.en: a forecast and a supply both trusted enough to plan with
branches.cn: 一份预报与一份供给都可靠到能据之做计划

intro.en: A Latin verb of saying and a prefix meaning before make the verb; English -able then turns the act of foretelling into a quality, and -ity and un- extend the family.
intro.cn: 一个表示「说」的拉丁动词和一个表示「在前」的前缀造出动词；英语的 -able 再把「预言」这个动作变成性质，-ity 与 un- 又扩展了这一族。

latinIntro.en: Dicere, praedicere and praedictio are all recorded Latin forms, so the family is documented rather than reconstructed; only the English adjective is recent.
latinIntro.cn: dicere、praedicere 与 praedictio 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，所以这一族词有据可查，并非重构；只有英语形容词是较晚才有的。

definition_zh: 预测；预言；预报
definition_en: a statement about what will happen in the future, especially one based on evidence, a model or reasoning
core_image: 一个人站在河边，手里拿着一张写着明天水位高度的纸条，纸条边缘还标着刻度
scene: 这里指「预测」。 The model's prediction was wrong by only two centimetres.
sceneCN: 这里 prediction 是「预测结果、预报」（第 1 个义项：关于未来的陈述）；句意：这个模型的预测只差了两厘米。图中可辨识物件：写有水位的纸条、刻度线、河岸与水位标尺。

pos.zh: 预测；预言；预报

senses.title: A statement about the future
senses.titleCN: 预测：对将发生之事的说法
senses.definition: a statement that something will happen, made before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 在某事发生之前说明它将会发生的陈述
senses.example: Her prediction that the bridge would fail proved right.
senses.exampleCN: 她关于这座桥会垮塌的预测被证明是对的。
senses.why: prae- means 'before' and dicere means 'say'. A prediction is literally something said before the event.
senses.whyCN: prae- 意为“在前”，dicere 意为“说”。prediction 字面上就是在事件之前说出的东西。

senses.title: The act of foretelling
senses.definition: the act or practice of saying what will happen, rather than the content said
senses.definitionCN: 说明将会发生什么的行为或做法，而非说出的内容本身
senses.example: Prediction is easy; being right is hard.
senses.exampleCN: 预言很容易，说准却很难。
senses.why: The -ion suffix can name an action. English keeps both readings, the act and its product, in one noun.
senses.whyCN: -ion 后缀既可命名动作。英语把“行为”与“产物”两种读法都留在同一个名词里。

senses.title: Scientific forecast
senses.titleCN: 科学预报：可检验的说法
senses.definition: a precise statement derived from a theory or model that observation can confirm or refute
senses.definitionCN: 由理论或模型推出、可被观察证实或否证的精确陈述
senses.example: A good theory yields predictions that can be tested.
senses.exampleCN: 好的理论会产生可被检验的预测。
senses.why: Science turns prophecy into a test: a prediction that cannot fail is not a scientific prediction.
senses.whyCN: 科学把预言变成检验：不可能失败的预测算不上科学预测。

senses.title: Model output
senses.titleCN: 模型输出：算出来的那个数
senses.definition: the value or outcome produced by a statistical or computational model for an unknown case
senses.definitionCN: 统计或计算模型对未知情形给出的数值或结果
senses.example: The prediction for next quarter is a small rise in demand.
senses.exampleCN: 对下季度的预测是需求小幅上升。
senses.why: Models produce numbers, and the industry borrowed the everyday word for them. The output inherits the word's forward-looking direction.
senses.whyCN: 模型产出数字，业界借用了日常词来称呼它。这个输出继承了该词“朝前看”的方向。

senses.title: Forecast of a trend
senses.definition: an estimate of a future quantity based on extending a current pattern
senses.definitionCN: 通过延长当前模式而得到的未来数量估计
senses.example: Population predictions suggest the town will shrink after 2030.
senses.exampleCN: 人口预测显示该镇在 2030 年后会萎缩。
senses.why: Extending a line is the simplest picture of prediction, and it explains why forecasters speak of trends rather than events.
senses.whyCN: 把线延长是预测最简单的画面，也解释了为什么预报者谈趋势而不谈单个事件。

senses.title: Prophecy and omen
senses.definition: in older usage, a declaration of future events attributed to inspiration or divine knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 较旧用法中指被认为来自灵感或神启的未来事件宣告
senses.example: The prediction in the old chronicle was read as a warning.
senses.exampleCN: 旧编年史中的那则预言被解读为警告。
senses.why: Before statistics, prediction belonged to prophets. The word still carries a faint trace of that authority.
senses.whyCN: 在统计学之前，预测属于先知。这个词仍带着一点那种权威的痕迹。

senses.title: Prediction in betting
senses.definition: a guess about a result on which money or reputation may be staked
senses.definitionCN: 对某个结果作出的判断，可能据此押上金钱或名誉
senses.example: His prediction of the final score won him the office pool.
senses.exampleCN: 他对最终比分的预测让他赢下了办公室的赌局。
senses.why: A bet makes a prediction costly. The word gains weight when being wrong has a price.
senses.whyCN: 下注让预测有了代价。当猜错要付钱时，这个词就变得有分量。

senses.title: Prediction versus explanation
senses.titleCN: 与解释相对：说将来而非说为何
senses.definition: in philosophy of science, the forward-looking counterpart of an explanation of what has already happened
senses.definitionCN: 在科学哲学中，与对已发生之事的解释相对的那个朝前的部分
senses.example: The same law can serve as explanation and as prediction.
senses.exampleCN: 同一条定律既可作解释，也可作预测。
senses.why: Philosophers split the two directions of a theory: backward to causes, forward to predictions. One law, two uses.
senses.whyCN: 哲学家把理论的两个方向分开：向后找原因，向前作预测。同一条定律，两种用途。

intro.en: Prediction comes from Latin praedicere 'to say beforehand', from prae- 'before' plus dicere 'to say, tell'. The noun is praedictio.
intro.cn: prediction 来自拉丁语 praedicere“预先说出”，由 prae-“在前”加 dicere“说、告诉”构成，名词为 praedictio。

items.en: dicere meant 'to say, tell, declare'. It is the source of dictate, dictionary and verdict, and it is not the same root as dicare 'to dedicate'.
items.cn: dicere 意为“说、告诉、宣告”。它是 dictate、dictionary、verdict 的来源，与 dicare“奉献、宣布”并非同一词根。

items.en: prae- 'before' plus dicere produced praedicere, 'to say beforehand, foretell'. The prefix is temporal, not spatial.
items.cn: prae-“在前”加 dicere 构成 praedicere“预先说出、预言”。这个前缀是时间性的，不是空间性的。

items.en: The action noun praedictio covered both 'a foretelling' and 'a proclamation'. Church Latin used it for prophetic declaration.
items.cn: 动作名词 praedictio 兼指“预言”与“宣告”。教会拉丁语用它指先知式的宣告。

items.en: English borrows prediction in the 1500s, first in religious and astrological writing about foretelling the future.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 prediction，最早见于关于预言的宗教与占星写作。

items.en: From the 17th century the word moves into natural philosophy, where a prediction must be testable against observation.
items.cn: 17 世纪起，这个词进入自然哲学，预测必须能被观察检验。

items.en: In the 20th century prediction becomes the standard term for a model's output, and machine learning makes it routine.
items.cn: 20 世纪，prediction 成为模型输出的标准说法，机器学习让它成为日常用语。

entries.definition: to say in advance that something will happen. The verb names the act; the noun names the act or its content.
entries.definitionCN: 预言；预测。动词命名行为，名词命名行为或其内容。

entries.definition: able to be foreseen because it follows a pattern. It describes the thing, not the forecast.
entries.definitionCN: 可预测的。它描述被预测之物有规律，而非描述预报。

entries.definition: dependence on a substance or habit. It shares dicere 'say' through Latin addictio 'a handing over', but has nothing to do with foretelling.
entries.definitionCN: 上瘾；成瘾。它经由拉丁 addictio“交出”共享 dicere，但与预言无关。

entries.definition: a statement of what is expected, usually from present data. It is close to prediction but commoner in weather and finance.
entries.definitionCN: 预报；预测。常指天气或金融，接近 prediction 但更常用于这两个领域。

entries.definition: an estimate of a future value obtained by extending current trends. It stresses method, not certainty.
entries.definitionCN: 推算；预计。强调延长现有趋势的方法，而非确定性。

entries.definition: a prediction claimed to come from divine or special insight. It carries authority that a scientific prediction does not.
entries.definitionCN: 预言。声称来自神启或特殊洞察，带有科学预测所没有的权威。

entries.definition: an opinion offered without firm evidence. It lacks the evidential base that prediction usually implies.
entries.definitionCN: 猜测。指没有坚实证据的看法，缺少 prediction 通常暗含的证据基础。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: pre- 'before' plus dict 'say' gives 'said before it happens', which is the whole meaning in two pieces.
normal.cn: pre-“在前”加 dict“说”，就是“在发生之前说出”，整个词义由两块拼成。

normal.en: The family predict, predictable, prediction and predictor all keep the same dict stem.
normal.cn: predict、predictable、prediction、predictor 全族保留同一 dict 词干。

normal.en: Scientific usage adds a test: a prediction must be able to fail.
normal.cn: 科学用法加了一条检验：预测必须有可能失败。

normal.en: Model prediction and weather forecast are the same forward arrow, one computed, one observed.
normal.cn: 模型预测与天气预报是同一支前箭头，一个算出来，一个看出来。

normal.en: The opposite word is retrodiction, a statement about the past made from present evidence.
normal.cn: 反面的词是 retrodiction（逆测），即用现在证据推断过去。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow drawn from today into an empty box marked tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭从今天射进标着“明天”的空格。

abstract.en: Picture a weather map where the isobars continue past the right edge of the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一张天气图，等压线一直画到纸的右边缘之外。

abstract.en: Picture a chess player saying the next three moves out loud.
abstract.cn: 想象棋手把接下来三步大声说出来。

examples.en: The report's prediction of a dry summer was correct.
examples.cn: 报告关于干旱夏季的预测是正确的。

examples.en: Every prediction from the model comes with an error range.
examples.cn: 模型的每一个预测都附带误差范围。

examples.en: A theory is valued for the predictions it makes possible.
examples.cn: 一个理论的价值在于它能带来哪些预测。

root: 拉丁 prae-“在前”+ dicere“说、告诉”→ praedicere“预先说出”→ praedictio；英语取 predictio(n-) 词干 + -ion。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all point one arrow forward in time, but differ in who is speaking and what backs the claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把同一支箭指向未来，差别在谁在说、凭什么说。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a note about tomorrow written today.
core.cn: 核心意象：今天写好的一张关于明天的纸条。

branches.en: STATEMENT AND ACT: the noun names both what is said and the saying of it.
branches.cn: 陈述与行为：这个名词既指说出的内容，也指说的行为。

branches.en: SCIENCE: a testable forecast and the philosophical pairing with explanation are the same demand for evidence.
branches.cn: 科学：可检验的预报与哲学上同解释的配对，都是同一个证据要求。

branches.en: CALCULATED FUTURE: model output and trend extension both produce a future number from present data.
branches.cn: 算出的未来：模型输出与趋势延长都用现在数据算出未来数字。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: prophecy is prediction backed by claimed inspiration rather than evidence.
branches.cn: 权威：预言是靠声称的灵感而非证据支撑的预测。

branches.en: STAKES: betting turns a prediction into a commitment with a cost.
branches.cn: 代价：下注把预测变成带成本的承诺。

intro.en: Prediction is pre- plus the dic- stem plus -ion. The prefix marks time, the stem marks speech, and the suffix turns the act into a noun.
intro.cn: prediction 由 pre- 加 dic- 词干加 -ion 构成。前缀标记时间，词干标记言说，后缀把行为变成名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin line is dicere 'say' → praedicere 'foretell' → praedictio 'a foretelling'. The same dicere also yields diction, verdict and contradict.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁线为 dicere“说”→ praedicere“预言”→ praedictio“预言”。同一 dicere 还产出 diction、verdict、contradict。

definition_zh: 占主导地位的；最突出的；占多数的；（生/遗）显性的
definition_en: most common, most powerful, or most noticeable in a place, group, or situation
core_image: 一片森林里同一种树占到七成，其他树种只能从缝隙里看见
scene: 在旧城区的街道上，三层砖房一栋接一栋。Three-storey brick houses are predominant here, and a glass tower appears only once in a whole block.
sceneCN: 这里 predominant 是「占多数的、最显著的」（第 1 个义项：在数量或可见度上占优势）；句意：这里占多数的是三层砖房，一整条街里只偶尔出现一栋玻璃高楼。图中可辨识物件：连排砖房、玻璃高楼、街道、店铺招牌、行道树。

pos.zh: 占主导地位的；最突出的；占多数的

senses.title: Most numerous or visible
senses.definition: present in the greatest number or most easily seen
senses.definitionCN: 数量最多或最容易看见
senses.example: Brick houses are predominant in the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 旧城区以砖房为主。
senses.why: The word joins prae- 'before, in front' to dominari 'to rule'. What is predominant stands in front of the rest: it takes the foreground by sheer presence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 prae-“在前”与 dominari“统治”连在一起。predominant 之物站在其余之前：它凭存在感占据前景。

senses.title: Having the greatest influence
senses.definition: having more influence or power than others
senses.definitionCN: 影响力或权力超过其他
senses.example: Market forces are the predominant influence on prices.
senses.exampleCN: 市场力量是影响价格的主导因素。
senses.why: Influence is the political half of the word: not how many, but who sets the terms. A view is predominant when the others must answer to it.
senses.whyCN: 影响力是这个词的政治一半：不看数量多少，而看谁定规则。一种观点 predominant，就是其余观点都得回应它。

senses.title: The main characteristic
senses.definition: of a quality, the one that most marks a thing
senses.definitionCN: 在标记某物上最强的性质
senses.example: Her predominant emotion was relief.
senses.exampleCN: 她最主要的情绪是宽慰。
senses.why: Applied to feelings and qualities, the word picks out the note that sounds above the others. It is not the only note, only the loudest.
senses.whyCN: 用于情绪与性质时，这个词挑出盖过其他的那一个音。它不是唯一的音，只是最响的。

senses.title: Dominant in a field
senses.definition: holding the leading position in a field or market
senses.definitionCN: 在某个领域或市场占据领先地位
senses.example: The company is predominant in online retail.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在网络零售中占主导地位。
senses.why: Business extends the ruling image to market share. Predominance is measured: the leader's share is larger than any rival's, so the metaphor becomes a statistic.
senses.whyCN: 商业把“统治”意象扩展到市场份额。主导地位可以测量：领先者的份额大于任何对手，隐喻于是变成统计数字。

senses.title: The most common species (ecology)
senses.definition: of a species, the most abundant or influential in a community
senses.definitionCN: 群落中数量最多或影响最大的物种
senses.example: Oaks are the predominant trees in this forest.
senses.exampleCN: 橡树是这片森林的优势树种。
senses.why: Ecology counts abundance and cover. A predominant species shapes light, soil, and shelter for the rest, so being numerous turns into being decisive.
senses.whyCN: 生态学计算丰度与盖度。优势种为其余物种决定光照、土壤与庇护，于是“数量多”变成“起决定作用”。

senses.title: The trait that shows (genetics)
senses.definition: of an allele or trait, the one expressed when paired with a recessive one
senses.definitionCN: 与隐性等位基因配对时表现出来的一方
senses.example: Brown eyes are the predominant trait in this family.
senses.exampleCN: 棕眼是这个家族中的显性性状。
senses.why: Genetics borrowed the word for the allele that appears in the phenotype. The expressed trait 'stands in front' while the recessive one stays hidden.
senses.whyCN: 遗传学借这个词指在表型中出现的等位基因。显现的性状“站在前面”，隐性的则藏起来。

senses.title: The leading color or tone
senses.definition: of a color or tone, the one that sets the overall impression
senses.definitionCN: 决定整体印象的那一种颜色或调子
senses.example: Blue is the predominant tone in the painting.
senses.exampleCN: 蓝色是这幅画的主调。
senses.why: In art and design the word describes the ground note of an image. Predominance here is visual weight, not count: a large field of one hue governs the eye.
senses.whyCN: 在艺术与设计中，这个词描述一幅画的底色音。这里的主导是视觉重量而非计数：一大片同色支配眼睛。

senses.title: Ruling or controlling (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, having supreme rule or authority
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：拥有最高统治权或权威
senses.example: The predominant power of the region was the old duchy.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的主导力量是那个老公国。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer, close to dominari 'to rule'. Modern English prefers dominant for political power and keeps predominant for prevalence and prominence.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层，接近 dominari“统治”。现代英语政治上多用 dominant，而 predominant 多指普遍性与突出程度。

intro.en: Predominant came from the language of rule. Its Latin ancestor praedominari means 'to be chief', built from prae- 'before' and dominari 'to rule'. English then softened the political edge into 'most common or most noticeable'.
intro.cn: predominant 出自“统治”的语言。它的拉丁祖先 praedominari 意为“为首”，由 prae-“在前”与 dominari“统治”构成。英语随后把政治锋芒磨成“最常见、最显著”。

items.en: The adjective is first recorded in the sense 'having ascendancy or chief power'.
items.cn: 这个形容词最早记录为“占优势、拥有最高权力”之义。

items.en: From praedominari 'to be chief or predominant', a compound of prae- 'before, in front' and dominari 'to rule'.
items.cn: 来自中世纪拉丁语 praedominari“为首、占主导”，由 prae-“在前”与 dominari“统治”复合。

items.en: dominari comes from dominus 'lord, master', which is built on domus 'house, household'. The lord is the head of the household.
items.cn: dominari 来自 dominus“主人、领主”，后者由 domus“房屋、家户”构成。领主就是家户之首。

items.en: domus is traced to PIE *dem- 'house, household', a reconstruction also behind domestic and domain.
items.cn: domus 被追溯到原始印欧语 *dem-“房屋、家户”，这一重构也见于 domestic 与 domain。

items.en: The sense widens from political power to qualities: a color, a feeling, or a species can be predominant.
items.cn: 义项从政治权力扩展到性质：颜色、情绪或物种都可以是 predominant。

items.en: Modern usage separates the twins: dominant stresses control, predominant stresses prevalence. Statistical and biological writing favor the latter.
items.cn: 现代用法区分这对孪生词：dominant 强调控制，predominant 强调普遍。统计与生物学写作偏用后者。

note.en: The first group is about the same dominus family and spelling; the second is about adjectives that also mean leading or most common.
note.cn: 第一组看同一个 dominus 词族与拼写，第二组看同样表示“领先”或“最常见”的形容词。

entries.definition: to be the strongest or most numerous. It is the verb behind predominant.
entries.definitionCN: 占主导；占多数。它是 predominant 背后的动词。

entries.definition: the state of being predominant. It adds -ance to the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 主导地位；优势。它是动词加 -ance。

entries.definition: controlling or most important. It shares dominari but stresses power rather than prevalence.
entries.definitionCN: 支配的；最重要的。它共享 dominari，但强调权力而非普遍。

entries.definition: existing or happening most often in a place or time. It stresses what currently holds sway.
entries.definitionCN: 在当地或当时最常存在或发生的。它强调当下占上风者。

entries.definition: first in rank or importance. It points to one leading thing, not to a majority.
entries.definitionCN: 等级或重要性第一的。它指一个领先者，而非多数。

entries.definition: found over a large area. It measures reach, not dominance within a group.
entries.definitionCN: 在大范围内可见的。它衡量覆盖范围，而非群体内的支配。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin prae- 'in front' plus dominari 'to rule', the dominant/predominant pair, and the ecology and genetics uses.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 prae-“在前”加 dominari“统治”、dominant 与 predominant 这对词，以及生态学与遗传学用法。

normal.en: Prae- means 'in front'. A predominant thing stands in front of the rest, so the eye and the count both find it first.
normal.cn: prae- 意为“在前”。predominant 之物站在其余之前，所以眼睛与计数都先遇到它。

normal.en: Dominari means 'to rule'. The word began as political power, then learned to describe majorities.
normal.cn: dominari 意为“统治”。这个词从政治权力开始，后来学会描述多数。

normal.en: Dominant vs predominant: dominant controls, predominant prevails. A dominant wolf leads; a predominant tree covers.
normal.cn: dominant 与 predominant：前者控制，后者普遍。dominant 的狼领队，predominant 的树覆盖。

normal.en: In ecology a predominant species is not just numerous; it decides the light and soil for everyone else.
normal.cn: 生态学中，优势种不只是数量多；它为其他所有物种决定光照与土壤。

normal.en: In genetics the predominant allele is the one that shows, standing in front of the hidden recessive one.
normal.cn: 遗传学中，显性等位基因是表现出来的那一个，站在隐藏的隐性基因之前。

abstract.en: Dominance is a relation, not a quantity: something is predominant only against a background of others.
abstract.cn: 支配是一种关系，不是数量：一物只有在其余之物的背景前才成其为主导。

abstract.en: Prevalence hides power: what is most common quietly sets the conditions for everything else.
abstract.cn: 普遍性隐藏着权力：最常见的东西悄悄为其余一切设定条件。

abstract.en: The word lets a color, a gene, and a culture share one grammar: whatever takes the foreground governs the frame.
abstract.cn: 这个词让颜色、基因与文化共享一套语法：占据前景者支配画面。

examples.en: Rice is the predominant crop in the region.
examples.cn: 水稻是该地区的主要作物。

examples.en: The predominant mood was one of cautious optimism.
examples.cn: 主要情绪是谨慎的乐观。

examples.en: Pine trees are predominant on the upper slopes.
examples.cn: 松树在上坡地带占优势。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑来的米能特”——扑过来的米特别多，占了大多数 → predominant 占多数的、主导的

root: 中世纪拉丁语 praedominari“为首”，由 prae-“在前”+ dominari“统治”构成；dominus 源于 domus“家户”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of predominant, all sharing one image: a thing that takes the foreground. The foreground can be counted (majorities), felt (emotions), seen (colors), or inherited (genes).
sensesIntro.cn: predominant 的八个义项共享一个意象：占据前景的东西。这个前景可以被计数（多数）、被感受（情绪）、被看见（颜色）或被遗传（基因）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one thing standing in front of and above the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一物站在其余之前、之上。

branches.en: PRESENCE: sheer numbers and visual weight put one thing in front.
branches.cn: 在场：数量与视觉重量把一物推到前面。

branches.en: INFLUENCE: a view or feeling sets the tone that others must answer to.
branches.cn: 影响：观点或情绪定下其余必须回应的调子。

branches.en: POWER: the old ruling sense survives in markets and in archaic political use.
branches.cn: 权力：古老的统治义在市场中与古旧政治用法里存活。

branches.en: ECOLOGY: abundance becomes decisive when one species shapes the habitat.
branches.cn: 生态：当一个物种塑造栖息地，数量就变成决定力。

branches.en: GENETICS: the expressed allele stands in front while the recessive stays hidden.
branches.cn: 遗传：表达的等位基因站在前面，隐性者藏于其后。

intro.en: Predominant is an adjective built on the verb predominate plus -ant. English adds -ly and -ance, and the base dominari also gives dominant, dominate, and dominion.
intro.cn: predominant 是动词 predominate 加 -ant 构成的形容词。英语加 -ly 与 -ance，词基 dominari 还生成 dominant、dominate、dominion。

latinIntro.en: Latin praedominari 'be chief' combines prae- 'before' with dominari 'rule', from dominus 'lord'. The same dominus family includes dominant, dominion, and domineer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 praedominari“为首”把 prae-“在前”与 dominari“统治”结合，后者出自 dominus“领主”。同一 dominus 词族还有 dominant、dominion、domineer。

definition_zh: 主要地；占主导地位地；绝大多数地
definition_en: mainly, or in a way that holds the largest share or the strongest influence
core_image: 一片林子里九成是同一种树，其余只在林缘零星几棵
scene: 集市上几十个摊位卖的全是同一种粗布，只有两个摊子摆着别的东西。The market is predominantly a cloth market, with only two stalls selling anything else.
sceneCN: 这里指集市在整体上以布市为主（第 1 个义项：大部分情况下、主要地）；句意为这个集市主要是布市，只有两个摊子卖别的东西。
